paras.zh: 这位特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官还向他在 2024 年大选期间创立的美国政治行动委员会 (America PAC) 捐赠了超过 7600 万美元，该组织在竞争激烈的参议院和众议院竞选中建立了庞大的选民投票率。

paras.en: The new contributions bring Musk's known federal political giving for the 2025-26 cycle to roughly $366 million, already surpassing the approximately $290 million he spent during the 2024 presidential election. The scale of the latest giving is historic: Musk's $158 million contribution to Senate Leadership Fund is among the largest known political donations by an individual in U.S. history.
paras.zh: 这些新捐款使马斯克在 2025-26 周期的已知联邦政治捐款达到约 3.66 亿美元，已经超过了他在 2024 年总统选举期间花费的约 2.9 亿美元。最新的捐赠规模是历史性的：马斯克向参议院领导基金捐赠了 1.58 亿美元，是美国历史上已知的最大的个人政治捐赠之一。

paras.en: The new figures were disclosed days ahead of a Thursday Federal Election Commission filing deadline, when political committees are due to report their third-quarter finances.
paras.zh: 新数据是在周四联邦选举委员会提交截止日期前几天披露的，届时政治委员会将报告其第三季度财务状况。

paras.en: The Senate Leadership Fund has spent heavily this cycle to defend the Republican majority, including in Texas, where GOP Attorney General Ken Paxton is running against Democrat James Talarico. Talarico leads Paxton 48.4% to 45.0% in FiftyPlusOne's polling average as of Oct. 12.
paras.zh: 参议院领导基金在本周期投入了大量资金来捍卫共和党多数派，包括在德克萨斯州，共和党总检察长肯·帕克斯顿正在与民主党人詹姆斯·塔拉里科竞选。截至 10 月 12 日，在 FiftyPlusOne 的民调平均值中，塔拉里科以 48.4% 比 45.0% 领先帕克斯顿。

paras.en: Musk separately gave $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, which supports Paxton. He also contributed $20 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, the leading super PAC supporting House Republicans, $10 million to the Republican Governors Association and $2 million to the Republican Attorneys General Association, the Times reported and Curnutte confirmed.
paras.zh: 马斯克另外向支持 Paxton 的 Lone Star Liberty PAC 捐赠了 1000 万美元。据《泰晤士报》报道，库纳特证实，他​​还向国会领导基金（支持众议院共和党的主要超级政治行动委员会）捐款 2000 万美元，向共和党州长协会捐款 1000 万美元，向共和党总检察长协会捐款 200 万美元。

paras.en: The trillionaire's footprint in Texas has expanded rapidly in recent years, with Tesla, X and The Boring Company now headquartered in the state and SpaceX growing its manufacturing and launch operations there.
paras.zh: 近年来，这位万亿富翁在德克萨斯州的足迹迅速扩大，特斯拉、X 和 The Boring Company 的总部现在都设在该州，SpaceX 也在该州发展其制造和发射业务。

paras.en: The political spending is also a sharp reversal from Musk's public comments last year.
paras.zh: 此次政治支出也与马斯克去年的公开言论大相径庭。

paras.en: "In terms of political spending, I'm going to do a lot less in the future," Musk said in May 2025.
paras.zh: “在政治支出方面，我未来会减少很多，”马斯克在 2025 年 5 月表示。

paras.en: At the time, Musk was stepping back after a highly visible role in President Donald Trump's administration and a public falling-out with the president. The two have since repaired their relationship, appearing together at several recent events.
paras.zh: 当时，马斯克在唐纳德·特朗普总统的政府中扮演了引人注目的角色，并与总统公开发生争执，之后正在退出。此后，两人修复了关系，并一起出现在最近的几次活动中。

paras.en: Musk also retains deep ties to the federal government through SpaceX, a major NASA and Pentagon contractor. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth last month also named him co-director of Project Meridian, a Pentagon panel studying the future of warfare.
paras.zh: 马斯克还通过 NASA 和五角大楼的主要承包商 SpaceX 与联邦政府保持着深厚的联系。国防部长皮特·赫格斯上个月还任命他为“子午线计划”的联合主任，该计划是五角大楼研究战争未来的小组。

paras.en: — Kevin Breuninger contributed to this report.
paras.zh: — Kevin Breuninger 对本报告做出了贡献。

articles.title: Trump 'not happy' with Kimberly Guilfoyle, weighs firing her

paras.en: President Donald Trump said Monday that he is "not happy" with Kimberly Guilfoyle, and is considering whether to fire her as U.S. ambassador to Greece.
paras.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，他对金伯利·吉尔福伊尔“不满意”，并正在考虑是否解雇她作为美国驻希腊大使。

paras.en: Trump's comments at the White House after a series of critical articles in The Wall Street Journal about Guilfolye's conduct before and after she became ambassador.
paras.zh: 这是特朗普在《华尔街日报》发表一系列批评吉尔福耶担任大使前后行为的文章后在白宫发表的评论。

paras.en: Asked directly by a reporter if he was weighing firing Guilfoyle, Trump replied, "Well, we're looking at it."
paras.zh: 当记者直接问他是否正在考虑解雇吉尔福伊尔时，特朗普回答说：“嗯，我们正在考虑。”

paras.en: "Yeah, we're not happy," the president said.
paras.zh: “是的，我们不高兴，”总统说。

paras.en: Guilfolyle previously was engaged to Trump's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr. After the couple broke up, the president appointed the former Fox News personality as ambassador.
paras.zh: 吉尔福莱尔此前曾与特朗普的长子小唐纳德·特朗普订婚。两人分手后，总统任命这位前福克斯新闻人物为大使。

paras.en: This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates.
paras.zh: 这是突发新闻。请刷新以获取更新。

articles.title: A unique shape, a 3D einstein tile, has been discovered

paras.en: It may look like a child’s Lego creation, but it’s a mathematical marvel. Researchers have just discovered a three-dimensional “einstein” tile—a special shape with unique capabilities.
paras.zh: 它可能看起来像孩子的乐高作品，但它是一个数学奇迹。 Researchers have just discovered a three-dimensional “einstein” tile—a special shape with unique capabilities.

paras.en: The finding follows a major announcement from 2023, when a new hat-shaped tile called an “einstein” rocked the popular mathematics world. David Smith, an amateur mathematician, discovered that shape. In an article later published in Combinatorial Theory, he and three other researchers—Joseph Samuel Myers, Craig Kaplan and Chaim Goodman-Strauss—proved that “the hat” was the first known example of a two-dimensional aperiodic monotile, also called an “einstein” (ein Stein roughly translates to “one shape” in German). In other words, the hat is a shape that can infinitely tile, or cover, a 2D surface without ever creating a repeating pattern. These building-block hats can be placed next to one another to create bigger and bigger shapes that also look like the hat. But each individual hat will be situated in a nonrepeating pattern that continues to change no matter how large the overall tiling is.
paras.zh: 这一发现是在 2023 年发布的一项重大公告之后发布的，当时一种名为“爱因斯坦”的新型帽形瓷砖震撼了流行的数学世界。业余数学家戴维·史密斯发现了这种形状。在后来发表在《组合理论》上的一篇文章中，他和其他三位研究人员——约瑟夫·塞缪尔·迈尔斯、克雷格·卡普兰和柴姆·古德曼-施特劳斯——证明了“帽子”是第一个已知的二维非周期单瓦的例子，也称为“爱因斯坦”（“爱因斯坦”在德语中大致翻译为“单一形状”）。换句话说，帽子是一种可以无限平铺或覆盖 2D 表面而无需创建重复图案的形状。这些积木帽子可以彼此相邻放置，以创造出越来越大的形状，看起来也像帽子。但每一顶帽子都会以不重复的模式排列，无论整体平铺有多大，这种模式都会不断变化。

paras.en: Now a researcher has taken this concept into the third dimension with a 3D shape dubbed the Chair44 monotile. Chair44 can infinitely tile a three-dimensional space by covering it without gaps or overlapping shapes. Moreover, that tiling is aperiodic, meaning that the pattern is never repeated. The finding was announced by Ioannis Tsiokos, director of Automorph, which he describes as an AI research lab.
paras.zh: 现在，研究人员将这一概念带入了三维空间，并设计了一个名为 Chair44 monotile 的 3D 形状。 Chair44 可以通过无间隙或重叠形状的覆盖来无限地平铺三维空间。此外，这种平铺是非周期性的，这意味着该图案永远不会重复。这一发现是由 Automorph 主任 Ioannis Tsiokos 宣布的，他将 Automorph 描述为人工智能研究实验室。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “I’m not a mathematician myself,” says Tsiokos, who is the sole human author of the preprint announcing Chair44. Tsiokos says he used Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 artificial intelligence model to write the paper and the OpenAI model ChatGPT-6 Astra to search for a 3D monotile, including to verify that the Chair44 monotile met the criteria for an einstein.
paras.zh: “我自己不是数学家，”Tsiokos 说道，他是宣布 Chair44 的预印本的唯一人类作者。 Tsiokos 表示，他使用 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.1 人工智能模型来撰写论文，并使用 OpenAI 模型 ChatGPT-6 Astra 来搜索 3D 单片，包括验证 Chair44 单片是否符合爱因斯坦的标准。

paras.en: Chair44 isn’t exactly the first example of such a monotile in three dimensions, according to Kaplan, a computer scientist whose research focuses on the intersection of mathematics and art. “For decades, we’ve known of an aperiodic monotile in 3D: a shape known as the Schmitt-Conway-Danzer biprism,” Kaplan says. That biprism, however—a kind of convex polyhedron—“obeys the letter of the law of aperiodicity but not the spirit,” making it weakly aperiodic, he notes. The Chair44 discovery, on the other hand, fulfills a decades-long quest to find a strong example.
paras.zh: 根据卡普兰（Kaplan）的说法，Chair44 并不是这种三维单块的第一个例子，卡普兰是一位研究数学与艺术交叉的计算机科学家。 “几十年来，我们已经知道 3D 中的非周期单瓦：一种称为施密特-康威-丹泽双棱镜的形状，”卡普兰说。然而，这种双棱镜——一种凸多面体——“遵守非周期性定律的字面意思，但不遵守精神”，使其具有弱非周期性，他指出。另一方面，Chair44 的发现完成了数十年来寻找有力例子的探索。

paras.en: “I’m pleased that we have the solution to what was, until recently, a nagging open problem in tiling theory,” Kaplan says. “We can also hope that this discovery will generate renewed excitement in the mathematics of tilings and encourage more young people to play around with geometry.”
paras.zh: 卡普兰说：“我很高兴我们解决了直到最近为止平铺理论中一个棘手的开放问题。” “我们还希望这一发现能够重新激发人们对瓷砖数学的兴趣，并鼓励更多的年轻人尝试几何。”

paras.en: To understand the geometric intuition behind the Chair44 shape, Tsiokos says, imagine a large cube composed of eight tiny cubes that are joined together. Next, remove just one cube. “Now you have a seven-cube chair,” he says.
paras.zh: Tsiokos 说，为了理解 Chair44 形状背后的几何直觉，想象一个由八个连接在一起的小立方体组成的大立方体。接下来，只取出一个立方体。 “现在你有了一把七立方体的椅子，”他说。

paras.en: The next goal on this journey is to create a bigger “chair” shape. That larger shape can be constructed by connecting four of these smaller chairs. To create a full tiling, just repeat this process over and over again, ad infinitum.
paras.zh: 这次旅程的下一个目标是创造一个更大的“椅子”形状。可以通过连接四把较小的椅子来构建更大的形状。要创建完整的平铺，只需一遍又一遍地重复此过程即可。

paras.en: As you build bigger and bigger chairs, however, you must arrange the smaller chairs in a nonrepeating pattern so that the resulting tiling will be aperiodic.
paras.zh: 然而，当你建造越来越大的椅子时，你必须以不重复的模式排列较小的椅子，这样最终的平铺将是非周期性的。

paras.en: “The trick” to ensuring an aperiodic tiling “is that you need to grow the chair in such a way that the behavior of the chair grows with it,” Tsiokos says. “To have this iterative, recursive building of chairs” requires making sure “that there are some sort of key locks between the chairs so that they form bigger and bigger chairs” that are made from a nonrepeating tiling pattern.
paras.zh: 齐奥科斯说，“确保非周期性平铺的技巧”是，你需要以一种让椅子的行为随之增长的方式来种植椅子。 “要进行这种迭代、递归的椅子建造”，需要确保“椅子之间有某种钥匙锁，以便它们形成越来越大的椅子”，这些椅子是由不重复的平铺图案制成的。

paras.en: When the hat monotile was discovered, it was so lauded that five researchers organized a two-day Hatfest celebration at the University of Oxford. Time will tell if Chair44 inspires its own celebration. For now, the reception to the finding has been mixed, largely because of Tsiokos’s significant use of generative AI in the proof.
paras.zh: 当单片帽子被发现后，五名研究人员在牛津大学组织了为期两天的帽子节庆祝活动，引起了广泛的赞誉。时间会证明 Chair44 是否会激发自己的庆祝活动。目前，人们对这一发现的反应褒贬不一，这主要是因为齐奥科斯在证明中大量使用了生成式人工智能。

paras.en: “There was a lot of human work that went into what went into Astra to do this,” Tsiokos says.
paras.zh: “Astra 需要做大量的人力工作才能做到这一点，”Tsiokos 说。

paras.en: Chaim Goodman-Strauss, one of the mathematicians behind the hat proof and an outreach mathematician at the National Museum of Mathematics, wrote a preprint reacting to the Chair44 results. In it, he described Tsiokos’s paper as having “hallmarks of an LLM-driven research paper,” including “so much irrelevant puff to push through.” Goodman-Strauss is one of at least two researchers who have now presented their own human-written proofs demonstrating that Chair44 is an aperiodic monotile.
paras.zh: Chaim Goodman-Strauss 是帽子证明背后的数学家之一，也是国家数学博物馆的外展数学家，他写了一份预印本，对 Chair44 的结果做出反应。在其中，他将齐奥科斯的论文描述为“法学硕士驱动的研究论文的标志”，包括“有太多不相关的内容需要推动”。古德曼-施特劳斯是至少两名研究人员之一，他们现在已经提出了自己的人工编写证明，证明 Chair44 是非周期单片。

paras.en: Tiling problems have been “a big part of my career,” Goodman-Strauss says. He has studied the shape that Tsiokos calls Chair44 for more than 30 years, he says, and is used to calling it “the L.”
paras.zh: 古德曼-斯特劳斯说，瓷砖问题一直是“我职业生涯的重要组成部分”。他说，他对 Tsiokos 称之为 Chair44 的形状进行了 30 多年的研究，并习惯称其为“L”。

paras.en: To explain how tiling with the shape works, Goodman-Strauss begins with an L-shaped building block. “You can make a bigger version of it out of eight little copies,” he says. “The problem is, that shape can also do all kinds of other crazy stuff,” he says. But because you can build a tiling from increasingly larger L shapes made up of smaller ones that are organized without repeating a pattern, each tile exists within what he calls “a supertile” that’s arranged in a unique configuration out of the smaller tiles.
paras.zh: 为了解释形状平铺的工作原理，古德曼-斯特劳斯从 L 形积木开始。 “你可以用八个小副本制作一个更大的版本，”他说。 “问题是，这种形状还可以做各种其他疯狂的事情，”他说。但是，因为你可以用越来越大的 L 形状来构建瓷砖，这些 L 形状由较小的形状组成，而无需重复图案，因此每个瓷砖都存在于他所谓的“超级瓷砖”中，该超级瓷砖由较小的瓷砖以独特的配置排列。

paras.en: Hence, Chair44 or the L is an aperiodic monotile in 3D.
paras.zh: 因此，Chair44 或 L 是 3D 中的非周期单瓦。

paras.en: Felix Flicker, a theoretical physicist at the University of Bristol in England, was one of Hatfest’s organizers. “I know a lot of mathematicians are unhappy with how the tile was discovered,” Flicker says. “The positive take is that we have a new important result.” The announcement comes after a summer in which AI models have repeatedly conquered many of math’s longstanding open challenges, including one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems. “The risk is that our jobs get reduced to sifting through AI slop in search of nuggets of gold,” Flicker says.
paras.zh: 英国布里斯托大学理论物理学家菲利克斯·弗利克 (Felix Flicker) 是 Hatfest 的组织者之一。 “我知道很多数学家对瓷砖的发现方式并不满意，”弗利克说。 “积极的一面是我们取得了新的重要成果。”这一消息是在今年夏天发布的，在这个夏天，人工智能模型多次克服了许多数学长期存在的开放挑战，包括七大千年奖问题之一。 “风险在于我们的工作会减少到筛选人工智能废品以寻找金块，”弗利克说。

paras.en: Flicker also wrote a Chair44 preprint, which he says aims to “provide the first human-written, human-readable, and therefore referee-able and defensible proof that Chair44 is a strongly aperiodic monotile.” (Even Flicker noted in his paper that he used Claude for coding and discussions in his study.)
paras.zh: Flicker 还写了一份 Chair44 预印本，他说该预印本的目的是“提供第一个人类编写的、人类可读的、因此可裁判且可辩护的证据，证明 Chair44 是一个强非周期性的单片。” （甚至 Flicker 在他的论文中指出，他在研究中使用 Claude 进行编码和讨论。）

paras.en: Tsiokos’s Chair44 paper “is just the first example of something that we’re going to be encountering a lot of” in terms of generative AI usage, Goodman-Strauss says. “One of the big lessons here in the age of LLMs is that we should remember all the [math] questions we asked before that were difficult to deal with.” Perhaps some of those problems can now be solved through the use of LLMs as a mathematician’s tool—although those technologies aren’t a substitute for human reasoning, he notes.
paras.zh: Goodman-Strauss 表示，Tsiokos 的 Chair44 论文“只是我们将在生成式人工智能使用方面遇到很多问题的第一个例子”。 “法学硕士时代的一个重要教训是，我们应该记住我们之前提出的所有难以处理的[数学]问题。”他指出，也许其中一些问题现在可以通过使用法学硕士作为数学家的工具来解决——尽管这些技术并不能替代人类推理。

paras.en: The use of generative AI to find new potential math research results isn’t going away. “It’s just that we have got to come to terms with what’s expected in terms of communication” of those results, Goodman-Strauss says.
paras.zh: 使用生成式人工智能来寻找新的潜在数学研究成果并不会消失。古德曼-斯特劳斯说，“只是我们必须接受这些结果在沟通方面的预期”。

articles.title: Lettuce engineered to produce meat proteins

paras.en: Perhaps you enjoy a burger in a lettuce wrap once in a while—but what if greens were also crucial to the patty? That’s the ultimate promise of new research showing lettuce can be engineered to produce myoglobin, a protein found in meat.
paras.zh: 也许您偶尔会喜欢吃生菜卷汉堡，但如果蔬菜对肉饼也至关重要呢？这是新研究的最终承诺，表明生菜可以被改造以产生肌红蛋白，一种在肉类中发现的蛋白质。

paras.en: Myoglobin (and its better-known relative hemoglobin) contains the compound heme, the red pigment in blood. Adding heme can give plant-based meat alternatives a meaty flavor and the ability to “bleed.” For example, Impossible Foods uses a compound called leghemoglobin (a heme protein derived from soybeans) to flavor its meat alternatives. But using myoglobin, which is found in animal tissue, could lead to vegetarian products that not only look and bleed like red meat but smell more like it, too.
paras.zh: 肌红蛋白（及其更广为人知的相对血红蛋白）含有复合血红素，即血液中的红色素。添加血红素可以赋予植物性肉类替代品肉味和“流血”能力。例如，Impossible Foods 使用一种名为豆血红蛋白（一种从大豆中提取的血红蛋白）的化合物来为其肉类替代品调味。但使用动物组织中的肌红蛋白可能会导致素食产品不仅看起来和血色像红肉，而且闻起来也更像红肉。

paras.en: In the study, published in Frontiers in Plant Science, the researchers describe how they got lettuce and tobacco plants to produce myoglobin for the first time, says lead author Alexia Groff, who worked on the project as a Ph.D. student at Imperial College London. The team engineered the plants’ photosynthesizing chloroplasts—the cell structures that typically turn sunlight into food—to make them do the job.
paras.zh: 在《植物科学前沿》上发表的这项研究中，研究人员首次描述了他们如何让生菜和烟草植物产生肌红蛋白，该项目的主要作者、博士生 Alexia Groff 说。伦敦帝国理工学院的学生。该团队对植物的光合作用叶绿体（通常将阳光转化为食物的细胞结构）进行了改造，使它们能够完成这项工作。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In previous attempts to make myoglobin using nonanimal sources such as yeast, the protein-production directions were placed in the nucleus’s genome, but Groff and her colleagues found that adding them to the chloroplast genome instead could yield more of it—perhaps producing myoglobin even more efficiently than animals do.
paras.zh: 在之前使用酵母等非动物来源制造肌红蛋白的尝试中，蛋白质生产方向被放置在细胞核的基因组中，但格罗夫和她的同事发现，将它们添加到叶绿体基因组中反而可以产生更多的蛋白质——也许比动物更有效地生产肌红蛋白。

paras.en: Right now yeast fermentation is the standard method of producing heme (as leghemoglobin), but the sterile environment and industrial equipment necessary for manufacturing can be pricey. Plants are much easier to grow. “Row-crop protein production would likely be faster than fermentation-derived production,” says Adam Leman, a principal scientist at the Good Food Institute, who was not involved in the study. “If existing crop-processing equipment can be used, costs for isolating and purifying a myoglobin-rich fraction could be quite low.”
paras.zh: 目前，酵母发酵是生产血红素（如豆血红蛋白）的标准方法，但制造所需的无菌环境和工业设备可能价格昂贵。植物更容易生长。 “中耕作物的蛋白质生产可能比发酵产生的蛋白质生产更快，”良好食品研究所的首席科学家亚当·莱曼（Adam Leman）说，他没有参与这项研究。 “如果可以使用现有的作物加工设备，分离和纯化富含肌红蛋白的部分的成本可能会相当低。”

paras.en: Lettuce is especially promising: the medium itself is edible, meaning lettuce-produced myoglobin could move more easily through the regulatory steps that can slow down the path from laboratory to market. A more streamlined process could also mean less money spent in production—and far less energy use.
paras.zh: 生菜尤其有前途：培养基本身是可食用的，这意味着生菜产生的肌红蛋白可以更容易地通过监管步骤，从而减慢从实验室到市场的路径。更简化的流程还可能意味着生产上花费的资金更少，能源消耗也大大减少。

paras.en: The meat industry is a voracious energy consumer: 60 percent of agricultural energy use comes from farming and transporting animal products. Making meat substitutes less resource-intensive is a step toward more sustainable food systems—even if it means making meat proteins in a vegetable.
paras.zh: 肉类工业是一个巨大的能源消耗行业：60% 的农业能源消耗来自农业和动物产品运输。降低肉类替代品的资源密集度是迈向更加可持续的食品系统的一步——即使这意味着在蔬菜中制造肉类蛋白质。

paras.en: “In science, there were things that we used to think were impossible that now are an everyday occurrence,” Groff says. “I’m very excited for what the future of this sector is going to look like.”
paras.zh: “在科学领域，有些事情我们过去认为是不可能的，但现在却每天都在发生，”格罗夫说。 “我对这个行业的未来感到非常兴奋。”

articles.title: Love blooms on a hostile colony world in As You Wake, Break the Shell

paras.en: One of science fiction’s oldest themes is its insistence that the future isn’t inevitable. Few contemporary authors embody that idea more than Becky Chambers, whose stories imagine alternative futures—not through grand revolutions or galaxy-spanning battles but through ordinary people trying to care for one another.
paras.zh: 科幻小说最古老的主题之一是坚持认为未来并非不可避免。很少有当代作家比贝基·钱伯斯（Becky Chambers）更能体现这一理念，她的故事想象了另一种未来——不是通过大革命或跨越星系的战争，而是通过普通人试图互相关心。

paras.en: As a defining voice of the “hopepunk” genre, Chambers has built a reputation for science fiction that prizes empathy as much as imagination. Her latest novel, As You Wake, Break the Shell, brings us to the hostile, unpredictable world of Fortune, where acid rain falls and billowing volcanoes shroud the horizon. The story follows a reclusive botanist and a spacefaring pilot across alternating timelines as they search for connection and purpose, attempting to navigate a life where Fortune has never favored the bold.
paras.zh: 作为“希望朋克”流派的代表人物，钱伯斯在科幻小说中赢得了与想象力同等重要的声誉。她的最新小说《当你醒来时，打破外壳》将我们带入了充满敌意、不可预测的财富世界，那里酸雨倾盆，滚滚火山笼罩着地平线。故事讲述了一位隐居的植物学家和一位太空飞行员跨越不同的时间线，寻找联系和目标，试图驾驭命运从来不眷顾勇敢者的生活。

paras.en: We caught up with Chambers to discuss a toxic planet’s world-building, scientific accuracy in storytelling and the motivational merits of unrelenting spite.
paras.zh: 我们采访了钱伯斯，讨论了有毒星球的世界构建、讲故事的科学准确性以及无情怨恨的激励优点。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: [An edited transcript of the interview follows.]
paras.zh: [编辑后的采访记录如下。]

paras.en: This story spends a lot of time on a colony planet with a poisonous atmosphere. What does designing an ecosystem teach you about designing a civilization?
paras.zh: 这个故事花了很多时间在一个充满有毒气氛的殖民星球上。关于设计文明，设计一个生态系统能教会你什么？

paras.en: Everything. It’s really important for me to start with what the environmental conditions are because that’s going to affect everything from what we’re eating, what we’re building houses out of, what kind of clothes we have—and all of those things, in turn, affect culture. There is so much about our values, our personalities, that are actually molded by the physical environments we exist in, both natural and constructed.
paras.zh: 一切。对我来说，从环境条件入手非常重要，因为这会影响一切，从我们吃什么、用什么建造房子、我们穿什么样的衣服——而所有这些反过来又会影响文化。我们的价值观和个性实际上是由我们所处的自然环境和人工环境塑造的。

paras.en: Starting from [the questions] “what do we have” and “what do we not have” is really important for me. Suppose someone’s eating a sandwich. What’s in the sandwich? It’s a throwaway line that seems like it doesn’t matter, but it’s actually really important to say whether or not there’s lettuce in this sandwich, because that does communicate a lot of information about how this world works.
paras.zh: 从[问题]“我们有什么”和“我们没有什么”开始对我来说非常重要。假设有人正在吃三明治。三明治里有什么？这是一句看似无关紧要的一次性台词，但实际上说这个三明治里是否有生菜非常重要，因为这确实传达了很多关于这个世界如何运作的信息。

paras.en: For this book, I had a really big table of crops [to reference], what are we growing, how are we growing it, what’s available and what’s not?
paras.zh: 对于这本书，我有一个非常大的作物表[可供参考]，我们种植什么，我们如何种植它，什么是可用的，什么是不可用的？

paras.en: Those are details I spend a lot of time sussing out before I really get into the thick of drafting the story.
paras.zh: 在我真正开始认真起草故事之前，我花了很多时间思考这些细节。

paras.en: What specific ideas inspired the scientific foundation for this story?
paras.zh: 哪些具体想法激发了这个故事的科学基础？

paras.en: Botany is the big one. I have always had an appreciation for plants but not any actual sort of technical knowledge about what it is that I’m looking at. So I did a lot of research for this book into how plants work, and specifically into seeds, which is a topic I have become fascinated by the more I learn about it. Seeds are a big part of this book, as are plants and the way they communicate with each other.
paras.zh: 植物学是一门大学科。我一直对植物很欣赏，但对我所看到的植物并没有任何实际的技术知识。因此，我在这本书中对植物的工作原理进行了大量研究，特别是对种子的研究，随着我对这个主题的了解越多，我就越着迷。种子是本书的重要组成部分，植物及其相互交流的方式也是如此。

paras.en: How does scientific accuracy influence your storytelling? Do you often find yourself molding the plot to fit the science, or vice versa?
paras.zh: 科学准确性如何影响你的故事讲述？您是否经常发现自己在塑造情节以适应科学，反之亦然？

paras.en: I look at science as partially a foundation but more of a tool that I use to color the world that I’m in. I want it to feel tangible and possible, but I’m very willing to take some liberties here and there for the sake of getting the feeling across.
paras.zh: 我认为科学部分是一个基础，但更多的是我用来为我所处的世界增添色彩的工具。我希望它感觉是有形的和可能的，但我非常愿意在这里或那里采取一些自由，以便让人们理解这种感觉。

paras.en: I tend to think of what I’m doing as more like impressionism than photorealism. If you think of something like Monet’s Water Lilies, for example, it doesn’t look like a real pond, right? But it feels like a real pond. And I often use a similar approach with my work. I am not necessarily painting you a picture of the cosmos as it actually exists, but what I’m trying to communicate is the sense of wonder and awe that I feel when I’m experiencing those things in the real world. So it’s a matter of getting the emotional quality of discovery across, and sometimes that does mean taking shortcuts.
paras.zh: 我倾向于认为我所做的事情更像是印象派而不是照相写实主义。例如，如果您想到莫奈的睡莲之类的东西，它看起来不像真正的池塘，对吗？但感觉就像一个真正的池塘。我经常在工作中使用类似的方法。我不一定要给你描绘一幅真实存在的宇宙图景，但我试图传达的是当我在现实世界中经历这些事物时所感受到的惊奇和敬畏感。因此，关键是要传达发现的情感品质，有时这确实意味着走捷径。

paras.en: With As You Wake Break the Shell, I kept it within the realm of “with sufficient technology, this could be possible.” Is it probable? Probably not. There are a lot of things that I gloss over because they’re not things that everyday people outside of science would know about or understand. We know [in the reality of the story] that there are giant space-dwelling creatures out there. We don’t need to know how it is that they evolved or what kind of world it is that they came from. Those are questions that interest me as a person who is into real science, but they don’t serve the story.
paras.zh: 在《As You Wake Break the Shell》中，我将其保持在“只要有足够的技术，这就是可能的”的范围内。有可能吗？可能不会。我掩盖了很多事情，因为它们不是科学之外的普通人会知道或理解的事情。我们知道[在故事的现实中]那里有巨大的太空生物。我们不需要知道它们是如何进化的，或者它们来自什么样的世界。作为一个真正热爱科学的人，这些问题引起了我的兴趣，但它们对故事没有帮助。

paras.en: This book has a knack for taking the unknown and making it feel familiar while making the familiar feel unknown, simply by showing it from a new perspective—for instance, that of an enormous, cargo-toting space behemoth. How do you get into the headspace of examining humanity from the outside?
paras.zh: 这本书有一个诀窍，即通过从新的角度展示未知的事物，使其感到熟悉，同时使熟悉的事物感到未知，例如，一个巨大的、载货的太空庞然大物的视角。你如何进入从外部审视人性的顶空？

paras.en: It’s a highly technical process that involves me sitting in my armchair and just staring at the ceiling and thinking about what it would be like to have a body other than mine, and just sort of deconstructing everything that makes me down to the raw components and trying to figure out what it is that’s necessary and what’s not.
paras.zh: 这是一个高度技术性的过程，我坐在扶手椅上，盯着天花板，思考拥有一个除了我自己之外的身体会是什么样子，然后解构一切让我只剩下原始组件的东西，并试图弄清楚什么是必要的，什么不是。

paras.en: I take a lot of inspiration from the natural world. I have a really keen interest in invertebrate life and in deep-sea life, and I have a real interest in animal intelligence that exists in nonmammalian creatures.
paras.zh: 我从自然世界中获得了很多灵感。我对无脊椎动物和深海生物非常感兴趣，而且对非哺乳动物中存在的动物智力也非常感兴趣。

paras.en: What would it mean to communicate through color? What would it mean to communicate through pheromones? What does the world feel like if you don’t have a sense of sight like we do? I just love taking any one of those traits and then expanding it to make something that we would recognize as a person, regardless of whether they physically look like us or not. How does that make you think about yourself? How does that make you think about existence?
paras.zh: 通过颜色进行交流意味着什么？通过信息素进行交流意味着什么？如果你没有像我们一样的视觉，世界会是什么样子？我只是喜欢利用这些特征中的任何一个，然后将其扩展为我们能够识别为一个人的东西，无论他们的外表是否像我们。这如何让你思考自己？这如何让你思考存在？

paras.en: As You Wake, Break the Shell is a love story as much as a space story. What did pairing those genres let you explore that you couldn’t do with either one on their own?
paras.zh: 《当你醒来时，打破外壳》既是一个爱情故事，也是一个太空故事。将这些类型配对可以让你探索什么是你单独使用任何一种类型都无法做到的？

paras.en: It allowed me the freedom to not segment any of the things I was thinking of into separate boxes. This was a really personal book for me in that I’m writing about everything I care about in this one. I’m writing about the natural world, I’m writing about society, and I am also writing about love, romantic love, and these are all things that are extremely important to me in my everyday life.
paras.zh: 它让我可以自由地不将我正在考虑的任何事情分成单独的盒子。这对我来说是一本非常私人的书，因为我在这本书中写下了我关心的一切。我在写自然世界，我在写社会，我也在写爱情，浪漫的爱情，这些都是我日常生活中极其重要的事情。

paras.en: We have a bazillion stories about “and then they lived happily ever after,” but I actually want to see what that looks like because it’s never that simple.I feel that the most interesting parts of a relationship are what happens “after,” and so that was what drove a large part of my decision to have [the book] be a split timeline, where it’s very clear from the jump that they’re going to be together a long time and we’re going to see all these different stages in what makes them them, because I do think that that’s an area that is underexplored.
paras.zh: 我们有无数关于“然后他们从此幸福地生活在一起”的故事，但我实际上想看看那是什么样子，因为它从来都不是那么简单。我觉得一段关系中最有趣的部分是“之后”发生的事情，所以这就是我决定将[这本书]分成一个时间线的很大一部分原因，从跳跃中很明显他们将在一起很长一段时间，我们将看到所有这些不同的阶段是什么让他们成为他们，因为我做认为这是一个尚未充分探索的领域。

paras.en: You’ve said before that you write the stories that you need to hear. What did you need to hear from this book?
paras.zh: 你之前说过，你写的是你需要听的故事。您需要从这本书中听到什么？

paras.en: I wanted to see a relationship that matched my own. Queer representation in media is better than ever in a lot of ways, and yet it’s still very rare to see anybody over their 20s.
paras.zh: 我想看到一段与我自己相符的关系。媒体中的酷儿形象在很多方面都比以往任何时候都更好，但仍然很少看到 20 多岁的人。

paras.en: By the time we started getting more stories about coming of age or people falling in love when they’re young, I was already too old for those stories. I was feeling a real frustration in not finding love stories that spoke to me where I am now in my life. It was one of those things of, “I guess I’ll just have to write it myself.”
paras.zh: 当我们开始看到更多关于成年或年轻时坠入爱河的故事时，我已经太老了，不适合这些故事了。我感到非常沮丧，因为找不到能对我现在的生活产生影响的爱情故事。这是“我想我必须自己写它”的事情之一。

paras.en: Your work has been described as “wholesome,” “thoughtful” and “heartwarming.” How much of your inspiration and motivation actually comes from spite?
paras.zh: 你的作品被描述为“有益健康”、“深思熟虑”和“温暖人心”。你的灵感和动力有多少实际上来自于怨恨？

paras.en: [Maniacal cackling] So much! I’m so happy you asked this question because so many people come at it from, like, “How do you maintain hope? How do you maintain the sense of coziness?” And the answer is that I am so pissed off all the time about everything. And honestly, so much of it does come from a place of looking at so many of the directions we are headed in the real world, so many of the decisions we are making about technology, about the environment, about how we organize ourselves as a society, feeling the crushing, overwhelming despair that I know we all feel and then just flipping that off and saying, “I’m sorry, I don’t accept that this is all there is and that it has to be like this.”
paras.zh: [疯狂咯咯笑]这么多！我很高兴你问了这个问题，因为很多人都会问这个问题，比如“你如何保持希望？你如何保持舒适感？”答案是我一直对所有事情都很生气。老实说，其中很大一部分确实来自于我们在现实世界中所走向的许多方向，我们正在做出的关于技术、关于环境、关于我们如何组织自己作为一个社会的许多决定，感受到我知道我们都感受到的压倒性的、压倒性的绝望，然后只是转过身去说，“对不起，我不接受这就是全部，也不接受它必须是这样的。”

articles.title: A quake on Mars may have set these rocks rolling
articles.author: Katherine Kornei

paras.en: Earthquakes frequently trigger rock falls. Now there’s solid evidence marsquakes can send boulders tumbling, too.
paras.zh: 地震经常引发岩石坠落。现在有确凿的证据表明火星地震也会导致巨石翻滚。

paras.en: Scientists mined high-resolution imagery of the Red Planet taken shortly after a recent temblor and found hundreds of new imprints left by tumbling boulders, researchers report September 2 in npj Space Exploration. Such rockfalls can be used as a proxy for seismic data, which is difficult to collect across the solar system.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 9 月 2 日在 npj Space Exploration 上报告称，科学家们挖掘了最近一次地震后不久拍摄的这颗红色星球的高分辨率图像，发现了数百个翻滚巨石留下的新印记。这种落石可以用作地震数据的代理，而地震数据很难在整个太阳系中收集。

paras.en: The data were collected with NASA’s InSight lander, which touched down on Mars in 2018. Over the next four years, its seismometer detected more than a thousand marsquakes. Many of those temblors originated in a region known as Cerberus Fossae, just north of the Martian equator. That’s a dynamic landscape riddled with slopes, cracks and rocks on the move, says Vijayan, a planetary scientist at the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad, India, who goes by a single name. “Thousands and thousands of boulders have fallen.”
paras.zh: 这些数据是通过 NASA 的 InSight 着陆器收集的，该着陆器于 2018 年登陆火星。在接下来的四年里，其地震仪检测到了一千多次火星地震。许多地震起源于火星赤道以北的一个名为塞伯鲁斯窝的地区。印度艾哈迈达巴德物理研究实验室的行星科学家维贾扬（Vijayan）说，这是一个动态的景观，布满了斜坡、裂缝和移动的岩石。 “成千上万的巨石倒塌了。”

paras.en: Vijayan and his collaborators focused on one well-detected marsquake captured by InSight that occurred in July 2019 just a few tens of kilometers from Cerberus Fossae. By comparing images taken in June 2019 and December 2020, the researchers discovered 27 new linelike features. Each was composed of tens to hundreds of distinct marks. These structures were most likely tracks created by boulders bouncing downhill, the team concluded.
paras.zh: Vijayan 和他的合作者重点研究了 InSight 捕捉到的一场地震，该地震发生在 2019 年 7 月，距离 Cerberus Fossae 仅几十公里。通过比较 2019 年 6 月和 2020 年 12 月拍摄的图像，研究人员发现了 27 个新的线状特征。每个标记都由数十到数百个不同的标记组成。研究小组得出结论，这些结构很可能是巨石下坡时留下的痕迹。

paras.en: Using historical imagery, the researchers calculated that only about two such features form each year on average in Cerberus Fossae. “We have statistics of previous boulder falls,” says Bivas Das, a seismologist at the Physical Research Laboratory and a member of the research team. Recording 27 new structures over a span of just 18 months is wholly unexpected, Das says. “That’s a big increase.” The nearby marsquake recorded by InSight was probably the instigator, the team concluded.
paras.zh: 研究人员利用历史图像计算出，Cerberus Fossae 每年平均只有大约两个这样的特征。 “我们有以前巨石坠落的统计数据，”物理研究实验室的地震学家、研究小组成员比瓦斯·达斯（Bivas Das）说。 Das 表示，在短短 18 个月内记录了 27 个新结构，这完全出乎意料。 “这是一个很大的增长。”研究小组得出结论，洞察号记录的附近的火星地震可能是始作俑者。

paras.en: Mysteries remain, however. All of the rockfalls occurred on the north side of a prominent valley in Cerberus Fossae, despite more boulders being located on the south side of the valley. “That puzzles us,” Vijayan says. The complex landscape of Cerberus Fossae might well alter how seismic waves travel, making it difficult to predict how shaking will impact different areas, he says. “The wave propagation is going to be complicated.”
paras.zh: 然而，谜团依然存在。尽管更多的巨石位于山谷的南侧，但所有落石都发生在塞伯鲁斯窝沟的一个著名山谷的北侧。 “这让我们感到困惑，”维贾扬说。他说，Cerberus Fossae 的复杂景观很可能会改变地震波的传播方式，从而很难预测震动将如何影响不同地区。 “波的传播将会很复杂。”

paras.en: Looking for such boulder falls elsewhere could help space exploration efforts, the team suggests. Human settlements would do best avoiding areas that are seismically active, and tumbling boulders can be the proverbial canaries in the coal mine, Vijayan says. “They’re like a proxy in the absence of seismic data.”
paras.zh: 研究小组表示，在其他地方寻找此类巨石坠落可能有助于太空探索工作。维贾扬说，人类住区最好避开地震活跃的地区，而翻滚的巨石可能是煤矿里众所周知的金丝雀。 “在缺乏地震数据的情况下，它们就像一个代理。”

articles.title: When climate change brings the heat, what happens to a mighty redwood?
articles.author: Allie Skalnik

paras.en: Towering coast redwoods are known for their resiliency, withstanding fire, fungus and rot to survive for centuries. But these ancient trees now may be vulnerable to a relatively recent foe: heat waves.
paras.zh: 高耸的海岸红杉以其生命力而闻名，能够抵御火灾、真菌和腐烂，能够存活几个世纪。但这些古老的树木现在可能容易受到最近的敌人的影响：热浪。

paras.en: As temperatures climb, photosynthesis slows in these iconic trees, researchers report September 22 in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences. Lab experiments show the rate of the sunlight-driven food making process in its needles roughly halves when temperatures rise from 30° to 40° Celsius.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 9 月 22 日在《地球物理研究杂志：生物地球科学》上报告称，随着气温上升，这些标志性树木的光合作用减慢。实验室实验表明，当温度从 30 摄氏度升至 40 摄氏度时，阳光驱动的针中食物制造过程的速度大约减半。

paras.en: Such a change usually indicates “severe levels of stress,” says Lily Klinek, an ecophysiologist at the University of California, Davis. That vulnerability can cause tree deaths that may jeopardize one of California’s largest stores of carbon, a shield against climate change.
paras.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的生态生理学家 Lily Klinek 表示，这种变化通常表明“压力很大”。这种脆弱性可能会导致树木死亡，从而可能危及加州最大的碳储存库之一，而碳储存库是应对气候变化的屏障。

paras.en: Coast redwoods (Sequoia sempervirens) live only in a narrow strip of coastal habitat from central California to southern Oregon, where temperatures are mild and fog is abundant. But recent heat waves have spiked temperatures in parts of their range to over 40° C.
paras.zh: 海岸红杉（Sequoia sempervirens）仅生活在从加利福尼亚州中部到俄勒冈州南部的狭长沿海栖息地，那里气温温和，雾气充足。但最近的热浪使部分地区的气温飙升至 40°C 以上。

paras.en: The impact of heat waves on photosynthesis has been studied in other tree species, with some faring better than others. But this is the first study to investigate how coast redwoods respond to the heat, says Troy Magney, an ecophysiologist at the University of Montana in Missoula.
paras.zh: 人们已经在其他树种中研究了热浪对光合作用的影响，其中一些树种的情况比其他树种更好。但这是第一项调查海岸红杉如何应对高温的研究，米苏拉蒙大拿大学的生态生理学家特洛伊·马格尼说。

paras.en: From July 2022 to October 2024, Klinek, Magney and colleagues repeatedly measured the performance of needles from redwoods in California’s Mendocino County. That period included two heat waves.
paras.zh: 从 2022 年 7 月到 2024 年 10 月，Klinek、Magney 和同事反复测量了加利福尼亚州门多西诺县红杉针的性能。那段时期经历了两次热浪。

paras.en: Typically, trees stay cool when small porelike openings called stomata allow water to evaporate, taking heat with it, similar to how sweat cools humans. But when conditions get too hot and dry, stomata close, retaining a plant’s moisture. Under extreme heat, the team found that needles reached up to 10 degrees C hotter than the surrounding air due to the dark needles absorbing ample sunlight. That suggests that the stomata were at least partially closed.
paras.zh: 通常情况下，当被称为气孔的小孔状开口允许水蒸发并带走热量时，树木就会保持凉爽，类似于人体出汗的方式。但当环境变得太热和干燥时，气孔就会关闭，保留植物的水分。在极端高温下，研究小组发现，由于黑色的针状物吸收了充足的阳光，针状物的温度比周围空气的温度高出10摄氏度。这表明气孔至少部分关闭。

paras.en: Those same pores are crucial for photosynthesis; it’s where the trees take in carbon dioxide — used to make food — and release oxygen. “They could essentially starve if they don’t have access to enough carbon,” Klinek says.
paras.zh: 这些毛孔对于光合作用至关重要。这是树木吸收二氧化碳（用于制造食物）并释放氧气的地方。 “如果它们无法获得足够的碳，它们基本上可能会挨饿，”克利内克说。

paras.en: It’s hard to investigate the impact of heat on photosynthesis in the field, though. That would take building a “heat chamber around a real-life branch or wait[ing] for a heat event to happen,” Klinek says. Instead, she climbed onto the roof of her car with a pole pruner and collected samples from about five meters high, in the lower canopy.
paras.zh: 不过，在野外研究热量对光合作用的影响很困难。克利内克说，这需要在现实生活中的树枝周围建造一个热室或等待热事件发生。相反，她用一把杆式修枝剪爬上车顶，在下部天篷约五米高处采集了样本。

paras.en: In the lab, the researchers subjected the samples to increasing heat to match the heat waves seen in recent summers and measured the resulting photosynthesis rates. Even though the samples were submerged in water, so had their stomata open and had full access to the ingredients for photosynthesis, the rate still declined. “They weren’t slowing their photosynthesis because of carbon starvation,” Klinek says.
paras.zh: 在实验室中，研究人员将样品置于不断增加的热量中，以匹配最近夏天出现的热浪，并测量了由此产生的光合作用速率。尽管样本浸没在水中，气孔打开并且可以充分获取光合作用的成分，但速率仍然下降。 “它们并没有因为碳匮乏而减慢光合作用，”克利内克说。

paras.en: For practical reasons, the study focused on younger coast redwoods, not the old growth giants. It’s difficult to reach even the lowest branches on trees more than 100 meters tall. “There are just fundamental limitations on what you can sample if you don’t have a jetpack,” says Christopher Still, an ecophysiologist at Oregon State University in Corvallis who was not associated with the study. Even so, the team’s results show that coast redwoods are “really temperature sensitive. You don’t see this as much with other species necessarily,” Still says.
paras.zh: 出于实际原因，该研究重点关注年轻的海岸红杉，而不是老树。 100多米高的树上，即使是最低的树枝也很困难。俄勒冈州立大学科瓦利斯分校的生态生理学家克里斯托弗·斯蒂尔（Christopher Still）并未参与这项研究，他表示：“如果没有喷气背包，你所能采集的样本就会受到根本性的限制。”即便如此，研究小组的结果表明，海岸红杉“确实对温度敏感。你在其他物种中不一定会看到这种情况，”斯蒂尔说。

paras.en: In the field, Klinek observed trees closing their stomata to preserve water. This suggests that in more realistic conditions, where a heat wave and drought hit simultaneously, lack of heat and water could make the slowdown “even more intense.” But more work needs to be done, she notes. “We still don’t know what the threshold is for irreversible damage.”
paras.zh: 在野外，克利内克观察到树木关闭气孔以保存水分。这表明，在更现实的条件下，即热浪和干旱同时袭来，缺乏热量和水可能会使经济放缓“更加严重”。但她指出，还需要做更多的工作。 “我们仍然不知道不可逆转损害的阈值是多少。”

articles.title: Scarred blood vessels may be one clue to APOE4’s Alzheimer’s risk
articles.author: RJ Mackenzie

paras.en: The gene APOE4 is the strongest common genetic risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease. But it’s still something of a mystery to researchers.
paras.zh: APOE4 基因是阿尔茨海默病最常见的遗传风险因素。但这对研究人员来说仍然是一个谜。

paras.en: Now, new work suggests one way the gene variant does its dirty work. It influences the production of scar tissue throughout vital vascular connections carrying blood to and from the brain, researchers report September 24 in Cell. This process may also contribute to the buildup of the protein amyloid-beta, which is thought to be one of the first signs of Alzheimer’s disease in the brain.
paras.zh: 现在，新的研究提出了基因变体进行肮脏工作的一种方式。研究人员于 9 月 24 日在《细胞》杂志上报道，它会影响将血液输送到大脑和从大脑输送血液的重要血管连接中疤痕组织的产生。这一过程也可能有助于β淀粉样蛋白的形成，这被认为是大脑中阿尔茨海默病的最初迹象之一。

paras.en: APOE4 is an allele, one of three slightly different, common forms of the APOE gene, which makes a protein that helps carry fats in the bloodstream. The variant is common among people who have Alzheimer’s disease. “If you had a room of 10 people with Alzheimer’s disease, and you asked how many of those people have the APOE4 allele, six of them would,” says neuroscientist Joel Blanchard of the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in New York City. Yet many people who carry APOE4 never develop the dementia-causing disease, leaving researchers trying to understand what the gene variant actually does to make the brain more vulnerable.
paras.zh: APOE4 是一种等位基因，是 APOE 基因的三种略有不同的常见形式之一，它产生一种有助于在血液中携带脂肪的蛋白质。这种变异在阿尔茨海默病患者中很常见。纽约市西奈山伊坎医学院的神经科学家乔尔·布兰查德 (Joel Blanchard) 表示：“如果房间里有 10 名患有阿尔茨海默氏症的人，你问其中有多少人携带 APOE4 等位基因，答案是其中有 6 人会携带。”然而，许多携带 APOE4 的人从未患上导致痴呆的疾病，这使得研究人员试图了解该基因变异实际上是如何使大脑更脆弱的。

paras.en: One clue came from people who seemed unusually resilient to that risk. In 2024, researchers examined more than 3,500 people, including some who carried two copies of APOE4 but had not developed Alzheimer’s. Genetic analysis showed that they had a mutation in their DNA that meant their blood vessels had far lower levels of a protein called fibronectin, a kind of cellular superglue that assists wound healing. The reserachers suggested that too much fibronectin could make it harder for the brain to clear amyloid-beta from the brain. A buildup of those plaques is a hallmark of the disease.
paras.zh: 一条线索来自那些似乎对这种风险异常有抵抗力的人。 2024 年，研究人员对 3,500 多人进行了检查，其中包括一些携带两个 APOE4 拷贝但并未患上阿尔茨海默病的人。基因分析显示，他们的 DNA 发生了突变，这意味着他们的血管中一种名为纤连蛋白的蛋白质的水平要低得多，纤连蛋白是一种有助于伤口愈合的细胞强力胶。研究人员认为，过多的纤连蛋白可能会使大脑更难清除大脑中的β淀粉样蛋白。这些斑块的堆积是该疾病的标志。

paras.en: That result pushed Blanchard and his colleagues to look more closely at blood vessels. “The prevailing thought in the field is basically that the Alzheimer’s disease is so bad that the blood vessels break down,” Blanchard says. ”But we wanted to ask the question: Is it the other way around?”
paras.zh: 这一结果促使布兰查德和他的同事更加仔细地研究血管。布兰查德说：“该领域普遍认为，阿尔茨海默病非常严重，以至于血管会破裂。” “但我们想问一个问题：情况是否相反？”

paras.en: Blanchard and his colleagues built an atlas that mapped gene expression — how DNA is read and converted into proteins — across the human brain vasculature at a cellular level. Stitching together data from three existing brainwide maps, their atlas represented 66,000 cells from 220 people. They team examined how this map differed in people with two copies of APOE4 compared with those with less harmful gene variants.
paras.zh: 布兰查德和他的同事建立了一个图谱，在细胞水平上绘制了人类大脑脉管系统的基因表达——DNA如何被读取并转化为蛋白质。他们的图谱将来自三张现有全脑图谱的数据拼接在一起，代表了 220 人的 66,000 个细胞。他们的团队研究了这张图谱在携带两个 APOE4 拷贝的人与那些危害较小的基因变异的人之间有何不同。

paras.en: APOE4 carriers had fewer pericytes, starfish-shaped cells that wrap around and stabilize blood vessels. They also had higher numbers of myofibroblasts, cells normally formed during tissue injury that pump out fibronectin, the team found.
paras.zh: APOE4 携带者的周细胞较少，周细胞是包裹并稳定血管的海星状细胞。研究小组发现，它们的肌成纤维细胞数量也较多，这些细胞通常在组织损伤期间形成，可产生纤连蛋白。

paras.en: The map offered a snapshot, but it couldn’t show whether the missing pericytes were actually transforming into myofibroblasts. The researchers turned to 3-D models of human brain tissue grown from stem cells. In models carrying two copies of APOE4, pericytes began taking on the characteristics of scar-producing myofibroblasts. The transformation also offered a possible explanation for the earlier clue from resilient APOE4 carriers: Myofibroblasts produce large amounts of fibronectin. And when the researchers prevented cells in their models from producing fibronectin, amyloid accumulation dropped.
paras.zh: 该图提供了一个快照，但它无法显示缺失的周细胞是否实际上正在转化为肌成纤维细胞。研究人员转向利用干细胞生长的人脑组织的 3D 模型。在携带两个 APOE4 拷贝的模型中，周细胞开始呈现出产生疤痕的肌成纤维细胞的特征。这一转变还为弹性 APOE4 携带者的早期线索提供了可能的解释：肌成纤维细胞产生大量纤连蛋白。当研究人员阻止模型中的细胞产生纤连蛋白时，淀粉样蛋白的积累就会减少。

paras.en: The researchers also found a possible trigger for the cellular switch. In the APOE4 models, signaling through the immune molecule TGF-beta helped drive pericytes toward the scar-producing state. Blocking that signaling in cell models and aged mice restored the proportion of blood vessels wrapped up by pericytes.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现了细胞开关的可能触发因素。在 APOE4 模型中，通过免疫分子 TGF-β 发出的信号有助于驱动周细胞进入疤痕生成状态。在细胞模型和老年小鼠中阻断该信号传导可以恢复被周细胞包裹的血管比例。

paras.en: The TGF-beta data are “particularly interesting,” because inhibiting the protein reversed some of APOE4’s effects on pericytes, says Abdel Ali Belaidi, a neuroscientist at the Florey Institute of Neuroscience and Mental Health in Parkville, Australia. But TGF-beta performs many jobs throughout the body, he says, making it a difficult molecule to target safely with a drug.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚帕克维尔弗洛里神经科学与心理健康研究所的神经科学家 Abdel Ali Belaidi 表示，TGF-β 数据“特别有趣”，因为抑制该蛋白可以逆转 APOE4 对周细胞的一些影响。但他说，TGF-β 在全身发挥着多种作用，这使得它成为一种难以用药物安全靶向的分子。

paras.en: And damage to the brain’s blood vessels is only one of the many ways APOE4 has been linked to Alzheimer’s. Other studies have shown that the gene variant alters inflammation and interacts with another Alzheimer’s-linked protein, tau. How all these changes lock together to link APOE4 so strongly to Alzheimer’s disease is a greater mystery than one study can solve. ”As a field, we’re all progressing toward an answer,” Blanchard says.
paras.zh: 对大脑血管的损害只是 APOE4 与阿尔茨海默病相关的众多方式之一。其他研究表明，该基因变异会改变炎症并与另一种阿尔茨海默病相关蛋白 tau 相互作用。所有这些变化如何结合在一起，使 APOE4 与阿尔茨海默病如此紧密地联系在一起，这是一项研究无法解决的更大谜团。 “作为一个领域，我们都在寻找答案，”布兰查德说。

articles.title: A Newer Class of Migraine Drugs Is Linked to a 40% Rise in Miscarriage Risk
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: Migraine is a very common neurological condition, and it occurs at even greater rates in women.
paras.zh: 偏头痛是一种非常常见的神经系统疾病，女性的发病率更高。

paras.en: Migraine attacks are notoriously difficult to treat: regular painkillers like NSAIDs and acetaminophen often just don't cut it.
paras.zh: 众所周知，偏头痛发作很难治疗：非甾体抗炎药和对乙酰氨基酚等常规止痛药通常无法缓解症状。

paras.en: In 2018, a new class of injected medications was approved for migraine treatment, as an option for patients who do not respond to mainstream oral treatments like triptans or ergotamine.
paras.zh: 2018 年，一类新的注射药物被批准用于偏头痛治疗，作为对曲坦类或麦角胺等主流口服治疗没有反应的患者的一种选择。

paras.en: But new research published in JAMA Neurology suggests this treatment may also raise the risk of miscarriage among expectant parents.
paras.zh: 但发表在《美国医学会神经学杂志》上的新研究表明，这种治疗也可能会增加准父母流产的风险。

paras.en: The medications are called CGRP-targeted monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), and they work by blocking CGRPs (calcitonin gene-related peptides). They tend to have fewer side effects than other migraine medicines, and fewer drug interactions.
paras.zh: 这些药物被称为 CGRP 靶向单克隆抗体 (mAb)，它们通过阻断 CGRP（降钙素基因相关肽）发挥作用。与其他偏头痛药物相比，它们的副作用往往更少，药物相互作用也更少。

paras.en: CGRPs are "inherently involved" in migraine attacks, but they also play a role in regulating blood flow, embryo implantation, and placental development during pregnancy.
paras.zh: CGRP“本质上参与”偏头痛发作，但它们也在怀孕期间调节血流、胚胎植入和胎盘发育中发挥作用。

paras.en: The new study, led by epidemiologist Anick Bérard of Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Sainte-Justine in Canada, suggests CGRP-blocking mAbs may interfere with a developing pregnancy, although the evidence is still quite limited at this stage.
paras.zh: 这项由加拿大圣贾斯汀大学中心医院的流行病学家 Anick Bérard 领导的新研究表明，阻断 CGRP 的单克隆抗体可能会干扰妊娠发育，尽管现阶段的证据仍然相当有限。

paras.en: The study is observational, which means it can only identify associations, not establish a cause.
paras.zh: 该研究是观察性的，这意味着它只能识别关联，而不能确定原因。

paras.en: Drawing from an existing patient dataset collected by private health insurers between 2018 to 2021, the researchers analyzed the first 20 weeks of 7579 pregnancies from mothers who, according to their health records, either had an official migraine diagnosis or had been prescribed triptan or ergot medications within the six months preceding their last menstrual period.
paras.zh: 研究人员利用私人健康保险公司在 2018 年至 2021 年间收集的现有患者数据集，分析了 7579 名母亲怀孕的前 20 周，根据她们的健康记录，这些母亲要么被正式诊断为偏头痛，要么在末次月经前的六个月内服用过曲普坦或麦角药物。

paras.en: Some of these mothers were also prescribed anti-CGRP mAbs (erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, or eptinezumab) or propranolol during or in the six months prior to their pregnancy. The researchers analyzed the data by estimated days of exposure to these two medications (hence 'person-time').
paras.zh: 其中一些母亲在怀孕期间或怀孕前六个月还服用了抗 CGRP 单克隆抗体（erenumab、fremanezumab、galcanezumab 或 eptinezumab）或普萘洛尔。研究人员通过估计接触这两种药物的天数（因此为“人次”）来分析数据。

paras.en: "Anti-CGRP monoclonal antibody exposure was associated with an increased risk of spontaneous abortion compared with unexposed person-time, while propranolol exposure was not," Bérard and team report.
paras.zh: Bérard 和团队报告说：“与未暴露的人相比，抗 CGRP 单克隆抗体的暴露与自然流产的风险增加有关，而普萘洛尔的暴露则不然。”

paras.en: Within the first 20 weeks of pregnancy, there was about 40 percent higher chance of miscarriage among mothers exposed to anti-CGRP mAb therapy, compared to no exposure, while propranolol was not associated with any increased risk.
paras.zh: 在怀孕的前 20 周内，与未接受抗 CGRP mAb 治疗的母亲相比，接受抗 CGRP mAb 治疗的母亲流产的几率增加了约 40%，而普萘洛尔与任何风险增加无关。

paras.en: While these results are concerning, if you are a migraine patient who wants to get pregnant, you should discuss your treatment and the risks with your doctor before making any changes to your medication regime.
paras.zh: 虽然这些结果令人担忧，但如果您是一位想要怀孕的偏头痛患者，您应该在对您的药物治疗方案进行任何改变之前与您的医生讨论您的治疗方法和风险。

paras.en: A study like this cannot show that a particular medication necessarily causes miscarriage.
paras.zh: 像这样的研究不能表明某种特定的药物一定会导致流产。

paras.en: Since these drugs are typically prescribed for treatment-resistant and severe migraines, it's possible that the migraines themselves may be involved in raising miscarriage risk.
paras.zh: 由于这些药物通常用于治疗难治性和严重的偏头痛，因此偏头痛本身可能会增加流产风险。

paras.en: There are several other limitations with the data.
paras.zh: 数据还存在其他一些限制。

paras.en: The records are based on a commercially insured US population, meaning the results may not apply to uninsured or publicly insured individuals, or people in other countries.
paras.zh: 这些记录基于有商业保险的美国人口，这意味着结果可能不适用于未参保或公共保险的个人或其他国家的人。

paras.en: Insurance records are also not necessarily collected with rigorous health research in mind: for example, the records used in this study don't account for how severe each individual's migraines were, whether the prescribed medications were actually taken, or whether pregnancies were planned.
paras.zh: 收集保险记录也不一定考虑到严格的健康研究：例如，本研究中使用的记录没有考虑每个人的偏头痛有多严重，是否实际服用了处方药物，或者是否计划怀孕。

paras.en: The authors say this study underscores the need for further research into the safety of anti-CGRP mAbs during pregnancy.
paras.zh: 作者表示，这项研究强调需要进一步研究妊娠期间抗 CGRP 单克隆抗体的安全性。

paras.en: "Given the increasing use of anti-CGRP mAbs for migraine prevention among individuals of reproductive age, further research is needed to evaluate their safety during pregnancy, including studies examining spontaneous abortion, fetal outcomes, and longer-term offspring outcomes," the authors write.
paras.zh: 作者写道：“鉴于越来越多地使用抗 CGRP 单克隆抗体来预防育龄个体的偏头痛，需要进一步研究来评估其在怀孕期间的安全性，包括检查自然流产、胎儿结局和长期后代结局的研究。”

paras.en: "Until more evidence is available, clinicians should consider the limited evidence on pregnancy safety when discussing anti-CGRP mAb treatment with individuals who may become pregnant."
paras.zh: “在获得更多证据之前，临床医生在与可能怀孕的个体讨论抗 CGRP mAb 治疗时，应考虑有关怀孕安全性的有限证据。”

paras.en: The research has been published in JAMA Neurology.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《JAMA Neurology》杂志上。

articles.title: Bones, Liver, And Blood Fats All Shift Abruptly at Menopause, Huge Study Finds
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: If puberty is like climbing a physiological cliff, then menopause may be like falling off one.
paras.zh: 如果青春期就像攀登生理悬崖，那么更年期可能就像从悬崖上掉下来。

paras.en: A new study, published in Nature Medicine, argues that the end of menstruation is not a gradual part of aging, as previously assumed, but an abrupt physiological transition.
paras.zh: 发表在《自然医学》上的一项新研究认为，月经的结束并不像之前假设的那样是衰老的逐渐过程，而是一种突然的生理转变。

paras.en: Using more than 300 million lab tests from over one million women, the new study identifies a number of sudden 'jumps' that occur throughout the body when menopause begins.
paras.zh: 这项新研究利用超过 100 万女性的 3 亿多项实验室测试，确定了更年期开始时全身发生的一系列突然“跳跃”。

paras.en: Some of the most obvious changes are to do with sex hormones, which the ovaries help produce, but there are also sudden shifts in bone health, liver function, kidney function, blood chemistry, and blood fats.
paras.zh: 一些最明显的变化与卵巢帮助产生的性激素有关，但骨骼健康、肝功能、肾功能、血液化学和血脂也发生突然变化。

paras.en: "Menopause reshapes female physiology, yet current understanding is
paras.zh: “更年期重塑女性生理机能，但目前的理解是

paras.en: limited by small longitudinal cohorts that characterize it as a gradual
paras.zh: 受到小型纵向群体的限制，将其描述为渐进的

paras.en: transition," explain the authors, led by molecular cell biologist Glen Pridham from the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel.
paras.zh: 以色列魏茨曼科学研究所的分子细胞生物学家 Glen Pridham 领导的作者解释道。

paras.en: Pridham and colleagues have instead used a computational framework to analyze the transition to menopause in two large cohorts of women, one in the United States and another in Israel.
paras.zh: Pridham 及其同事使用计算框架来分析两组女性（一组来自美国，另一组来自以色列）向更年期的转变。

paras.en: Their method is designed to disentangle a person's chronological age from their reproductive timeline, which has previously complicated population-wide studies.
paras.zh: 他们的方法旨在将一个人的实际年龄与其生殖时间线分开，这使得之前的人口范围研究变得复杂。

paras.en: According to both cohorts, the final menstrual period is marked by a "step-like physiological cliff" across nearly all physiological systems.
paras.zh: 根据这两个队列，最后一次月经期的特点是几乎所有生理系统都出现“阶梯状的生理悬崖”。

paras.en: The changes are most pronounced in systems such as bone metabolism, liver tests, and lipid handling.
paras.zh: 这些变化在骨代谢、肝脏测试和脂质处理等系统中最为明显。

paras.en: "While prior longitudinal studies… have established bone loss and specific hormonal surges, the scale of this study, covering 90 types of tests, demonstrates that this transition is sharp and systemic," the authors conclude.
paras.zh: 作者总结道：“虽然之前的纵向研究……已经确定了骨质流失和特定的激素激增，但这项涵盖 90 种测试的研究规模表明，这种转变是急剧且系统性的。”

paras.en: In the US dataset, for instance, 52 of 90 laboratory tests showed a statistically significant and sudden change with menopause.
paras.zh: 例如，在美国的数据集中，90 项实验室测试中有 52 项显示出更年期带来的统计上显着的突然变化。

paras.en: "Notably," the authors add, "we find that male individuals lack these abrupt physiological shifts, suggesting that the cliff is a consequence of the menopausal transition rather than general aging."
paras.zh: “值得注意的是，”作者补充道，“我们发现男性个体缺乏这些突然的生理变化，这表明悬崖是更年期过渡而不是普遍衰老的结果。”

paras.en: Not everyone agrees that these changes should be described as a cliff.
paras.zh: 并非所有人都同意这些变化应该被描述为悬崖。

paras.en: Martha Hickey, an obstetrics and gynecology professor at the University of Melbourne in Australia, who was not involved in the study, says that this description is "potentially alarming for women and implies a dramatic physical and mental decline, which this study does not demonstrate."
paras.zh: 澳大利亚墨尔本大学妇产科教授玛莎·希基（Martha Hickey）并未参与这项研究，她表示，这种描述“可能会让女性感到震惊，并暗示身体和智力会急剧下降，而这项研究并未证明这一点。”

paras.en: Other studies which show widespread changes at menopause have reframed this transition not as a step down, like 'reproductive retirement', but as a sudden 'career change' for the body and brain.
paras.zh: 其他显示更年期广泛变化的研究将这种转变重新定义为身体和大脑的突然“职业转变”，而不是像“生育退休”那样的退步。

paras.en: During a person's reproductive years, the ovaries work to develop follicles that produce and release eggs.
paras.zh: 在人的生育年龄，卵巢会发育出产生和释放卵子的卵泡。

paras.en: The hormones that these organs release, such as estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone, have widespread effects on the rest of the body, and this could have important ramifications for a person's health as they age.
paras.zh: 这些器官释放的激素，如雌激素、黄体酮和睾酮，对身体的其他部位有广泛的影响，随着年龄的增长，这可能会对一个人的健康产生重要的影响。

paras.en: At menopause, one hormone in particular seems to pull a lot of strings: estrogen.
paras.zh: 在更年期，一种激素似乎起着特别重要的作用：雌激素。

paras.en: "The systems where the most significant changes were seen (e.g. bone health, or the liver) are very sensitive to estrogen, and systems that didn't show detectable changes have a much weaker known link to estrogen," explains physiologist Mia Schaumberg, who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: “观察到最显着变化的系统（例如骨骼健康或肝脏）对雌激素非常敏感，而没有表现出可检测到的变化的系统与雌激素的已知联系要弱得多，”未参与这项研究的生理学家米娅·绍姆伯格（Mia Schaumberg）解释道。

paras.en: Schaumberg, from Australia's University of the Sunshine Coast, also finds another result interesting. In the study, around 15 and 12 years before the end of menstruation, the Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) and oestradiol show signs of decline.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚阳光海岸大学的绍姆伯格也发现了另一个有趣的结果。研究中，在月经结束前约 15 年和 12 年，抗苗勒氏管激素 (AMH) 和雌二醇出现下降迹象。

paras.en: Whereas around 14 years before menopause, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) increases.
paras.zh: 而在绝经前大约 14 年，卵泡刺激素 (FSH) 会增加。

paras.en: "This shows that systemic changes experienced during menopause could be predicted by hormone changes much sooner than originally thought," says Schaumberg.
paras.zh: “这表明，更年期期间经历的全身变化可以通过激素变化来预测，比最初想象的要早得多，”绍姆伯格说。

paras.en: The findings are supported by recent research among mice, which suggests that the ovaries begin aging decades before menopause begins.
paras.zh: 这些发现得到了最近对小鼠的研究的支持，该研究表明卵巢在绝经开始前几十年就开始老化。

paras.en: But this study is only observational, and health scientist Andrew Shelling from the University of Auckland in New Zealand warns that while these results are interesting, they are not conclusive.
paras.zh: 但这项研究只是观察性的，新西兰奥克兰大学的健康科学家安德鲁·谢林警告说，虽然这些结果很有趣，但它们并不是结论性的。

paras.en: Menopause is a major transition in human health that we still know so little about.
paras.zh: 更年期是人类健康的一个重大转变，但我们对此仍然知之甚少。

paras.en: "The study opens a new way of thinking about menopause and provides a new framework for future research," says Shelling, who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: “这项研究开启了一种思考更年期的新方式，并为未来的研究提供了一个新的框架，”未参与这项研究的谢林说。

paras.en: "As we work to better understand how menopause reshapes female physiology, this research is likely to be the beginning of many new discoveries to come."
paras.zh: “随着我们努力更好地了解更年期如何重塑女性生理机能，这项研究很可能成为未来许多新发现的开始。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Medicine.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然医学》杂志上。

articles.title: Experts Identified The Gravest Health Threats Facing Humanity – Two Have 'Extinction Potential'
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: If there's one thing the COVID-19 pandemic taught us, it's that the world isn't always as prepared for a crisis as we might think.
paras.zh: 如果说 COVID-19 大流行教会了我们一件事，那就是世界并不总是像我们想象的那样为危机做好准备。

paras.en: Now, in a sweeping international assessment published in The Lancet, a team of dozens of scientific experts has cataloged the dangers of 17 major global health threats faced by humanity this century – and preparedness is a key theme of their findings.
paras.zh: 现在，在《柳叶刀》上发表的一项全面的国际评估中，由数十名科学专家组成的团队列出了本世纪人类面临的 17 种主要全球健康威胁的危险，而做好准备是他们研究结果的一个关键主题。

paras.en: While it's a sobering review, the key message is that the dangers of global catastrophes can be mitigated and managed, but only if society takes action now.
paras.zh: 虽然这是一次发人深省的审查，但关键信息是，全球灾难的危险是可以减轻和管理的，但前提是社会现在就采取行动。

paras.en: "The striking finding is not only the scale of these threats, but that humanity still has the agency to act," says physician and health economist Christopher JL Murray from the University of Washington, the co-chair of The Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health.
paras.zh: 华盛顿大学的医生兼健康经济学家、《柳叶刀》21 世纪全球健康威胁委员会联合主席克里斯托弗·JL 默里 (Christopher JL Murray) 表示：“令人震惊的发现不仅在于这些威胁的规模，还在于人类仍然有采取行动的能力。”

paras.en: "Across all 17 catastrophic threats, the decisions made by leaders today will shape the health and well-being of the next generation."
paras.zh: “在所有 17 种灾难性威胁中，领导人今天做出的决定将影响下一代的健康和福祉。”

paras.en: In their study, the researchers used modeling to estimate how much death and disability could potentially be avoided for each threat between 2025 and 2100, measured in disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs).
paras.zh: 在他们的研究中，研究人员使用模型来估计 2025 年至 2100 年间每种威胁可以避免多少死亡和残疾，以残疾调整生命年 (DALY) 来衡量。

paras.en: "The estimates highlight how much health loss could be avoided in each area," Murray says.
paras.zh: “这些估计强调了每个地区可以避免多少健康损失，”默里说。

paras.en: "Some are already imposing substantial health burdens today, while others carry a real danger if they materialize."
paras.zh: “今天，有些人已经造成了巨大的健康负担，而另一些人一旦成为现实，就会带来真正的危险。”

paras.en: Of the most dangerous threats, the researchers say two in particular deserve special attention, rating them as carrying "extinction potential" for humanity between now and 2100, despite their ultimately low probability.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，在最危险的威胁中，有两种威胁尤其值得特别关注，并将它们评为从现在到 2100 年之间对人类具有“灭绝潜力”，尽管它们最终的可能性很低。

paras.en: "These were malicious AI, including using AI to create new bioweapons, and nuclear conflict with nuclear famine," the researchers explain in their report, noting that other potentially extinction-level dangers, such as asteroid strikes or supervolcano eruptions, were discounted due to their very low probability of occurring this century.
paras.zh: 研究人员在报告中解释说：“这些都是恶意人工智能，包括利用人工智能制造新的生物武器，以及核冲突和核饥荒。”他们指出，其他潜在的灭绝级别的危险，例如小行星撞击或超级火山喷发，由于本世纪发生的可能性非常低，因此被忽视了。

paras.en: Another possible event with hypothesized extinction potential for humanity – the creation of 'mirror life' – was similarly left out because it has not yet been developed, and despite the theoretical dangers to human health, it's too early to quantify them.
paras.zh: 另一种可能对人类具有灭绝潜力的事件——“镜子生命”的创造——同样被排除在外，因为它尚未开发出来，尽管理论上对人类健康存在危险，但现在量化它们还为时过早。

paras.en: After the special cases of malicious AI and nuclear conflict, the researchers identified 15 major catastrophic risks, each associated with more than 1 billion potentially avoidable DALYs between now and 2100.
paras.zh: 在恶意人工智能和核冲突的特殊案例之后，研究人员确定了 15 种重大灾难性风险，每一种风险都与从现在到 2100 年期间超过 10 亿个可能可避免的伤残调整生命年 (DALY) 相关。

paras.en: "For reference, 1 billion DALYs is equivalent to two COVID-19 pandemics," the researchers write, "showing that these are critical threats for governments and the global community to address."
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“作为参考，10 亿伤残调整生命年相当于两次 COVID-19 大流行，这表明这些是政府和国际社会需要应对的重大威胁。”

paras.en: Among this category, the researchers identified: air pollution, antimicrobial resistance, childhood malnutrition, climate change, the collapse of international aid funding for health, conventional armed conflict, high alcohol use, high blood pressure, income inequality, low educational attainment, naturally occurring pandemics, obesity, poor mental health, smoking, and unhealthy aging.
paras.zh: 研究人员在这一类别中发现了：空气污染、抗菌素耐药性、儿童营养不良、气候变化、国际卫生援助资金崩溃、常规武装冲突、大量饮酒、高血压、收入不平等、教育程度低、自然发生的流行病、肥胖、心理健康状况不佳、吸烟和不健康的老龄化。

paras.en: Of these, the threat with the largest potentially avoidable burden was obesity (including the health effects of high BMI, poor diet, and low physical activity), with an estimated 23.1 billion DALYs – corresponding to about 46 COVID-19 pandemics – being the difference between the best- and worst-case scenarios by 2100.
paras.zh: 其中，最大的潜在可避免负担的威胁是肥胖（包括高 BMI、不良饮食和低体力活动对健康的影响），预计 231 亿伤残调整生命年（相当于约 46 次 COVID-19 大流行）是到 2100 年最好情况和最坏情况之间的差异。

paras.en: After obesity, the largest potentially avoidable health burdens were low educational attainment and income inequality, with higher rates of education projected to reduce the burden of disease both by improving people's health and slowing population growth.
paras.zh: 除了肥胖之外，最大的可避免的健康负担是教育程度低和收入不平等，预计较高的教育率可以通过改善人们的健康和减缓人口增长来减轻疾病负担。

paras.en: Under the researchers' baseline forecast, the total global burden of disease and injury between 2025 and 2100 amounts to an estimated 246 billion DALYs – equivalent to roughly 500 COVID-19 pandemics.
paras.zh: 根据研究人员的基线预测，2025 年至 2100 年间，全球疾病和伤害总负担估计达 2,460 亿伤残调整生命年，相当于大约 500 次 COVID-19 大流行。

paras.en: Such is the scale of the issues at stake – but it's important to note that, since the burden of each threat was calculated individually, the total burdens can't be added together like that, as it would over-count the overlap in health problems faced by individuals.
paras.zh: 这就是所涉问题的规模，但值得注意的是，由于每个威胁的负担都是单独计算的，因此总负担不能像这样加在一起，因为这会过多计算个人面临的健康问题的重叠部分。

paras.en: On that note, one of the key points the researchers emphasize is just how interconnected many of these health dangers are, and how solving these problems calls for a long-term and multi-faceted approach that doesn't simply combat individual problems in isolation.
paras.zh: 在这一点上，研究人员强调的关键点之一是，许多健康危险是如何相互关联的，以及解决这些问题如何需要采取长期和多方面的方法，而不仅仅是孤立地解决个别问题。

paras.en: Instead, the researchers make three key recommendations, calling for governments to build and fund threat-ready health systems, to dramatically increase investment in breakthrough innovation (in areas like health, climate, and technology), and to create a "Monitor of 21st Century Global Threats to Health" to continually track and update threat assessments.
paras.zh: 相反，研究人员提出了三项关键建议，呼吁各国政府建立并资助应对威胁的卫生系统，大幅增加对突破性创新（在健康、气候和技术等领域）的投资，并创建“21世纪全球健康威胁监测器”以持续跟踪和更新威胁评估。

paras.en: "Perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms," The Lancet's editors write in an accompanying editorial perspective.
paras.zh: “也许该委员会最重要的贡献是使全球健康超越对个人危害的考虑，”《柳叶刀》的编辑在随附的社论观点中写道。

paras.en: "The unpleasant reality is that the threats we face are multiple, complex, and difficult… We believe this Commission can catalyze international, regional, and national actions to protect and strengthen the future of health and humanity. Doing so will require all of us to think much more broadly about where the biggest threats lie."
paras.zh: “令人不快的现实是，我们面临的威胁是多重、复杂和困难的……我们相信，该委员会可以促进国际、区域和国家行动，以保护和加强健康和人类的未来。这样做需要我们所有人更广泛地思考最大的威胁在哪里。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in The Lancet.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《柳叶刀》上。

articles.title: NASA captures a stunning transformation in Australia's red outback

paras.en: NASA captures a stunning transformation in Australia's red outback
paras.zh: 美国宇航局 (NASA) 捕捉到澳大利亚红色内陆地区令人惊叹的转变

paras.en: - Australia's normally dry, rust-colored outback has erupted into a spectacular carpet of wildflowers after unusually heavy rains, potentially producing its most impressive bloom in nearly 20 years. NASA satellite images capture the stunning transformation, which has even brought rare flowers to the grounds of a remote deep-space observatory.
paras.zh: - 澳大利亚一向干燥、铁锈色的内陆地区在一场异常大雨之后，突然绽放出壮观的野花地毯，有可能绽放出近 20 年来最令人印象深刻的花朵。美国宇航局的卫星图像捕捉到了这一令人惊叹的转变，甚至为偏远的深空天文台的地面带来了罕见的花朵。

paras.en: A spectacular explosion of wildflowers has transformed the normally dry, rust-colored landscape of Western Australia into a vibrant patchwork of green and colorful blooms. The remarkable display followed months of unusually wet weather, awakening seeds that had been lying dormant beneath the soil.
paras.zh: 壮观的野花绽放，将西澳大利亚通常干燥的铁锈色景观变成了充满活力的绿色和多彩花朵拼凑而成。这次非凡的展示是在几个月异常潮湿的天气之后发生的，唤醒了一直休眠在土壤下的种子。

paras.en: By late winter 2026 in the Southern Hemisphere, large stretches of the region's arid shrubland were covered in flowers. Local experts believe this could be the most impressive wildflower season the area has experienced in nearly 20 years.
paras.zh: 到 2026 年冬末，南半球该地区大片干旱的灌木丛已被鲜花覆盖。当地专家认为，这可能是该地区近 20 年来最令人印象深刻的野花季节。

paras.en: NASA satellite imagery reveals just how dramatically the landscape changed in a single year.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局的卫星图像揭示了一年内地貌发生了多么巨大的变化。

paras.en: NASA Satellite Images Reveal a Dramatic Transformation
paras.zh: 美国宇航局卫星图像揭示了巨大的转变

paras.en: The images above were collected by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) aboard the NASA-USGS Landsat 8 satellite. They show the same part of Western Australia in late August 2025 (left) and late August 2026 (right), highlighting the striking increase in vegetation following the unusually wet conditions.
paras.zh: 上面的图像是由 NASA-USGS Landsat 8 卫星上的 OLI（操作陆地成像仪）收集的。它们显示了 2025 年 8 月下旬（左）和 2026 年 8 月下旬（右）西澳大利亚州的同一部分，突出显示了异常潮湿的条件后植被的显着增加。

paras.en: The location is in the Murchison region, approximately 600 kilometers (370 miles) north of Perth. This remote stretch of the Australian outback is an important grazing area for sheep and cattle, with a landscape typically dominated by hardy plants adapted to limited rainfall.
paras.zh: 该地点位于珀斯以北约 600 公里（370 英里）处的默奇森地区。澳大利亚内陆的这片偏远地区是牛羊的重要放牧区，这里的景观通常以适应有限降雨的耐寒植物为主。

paras.en: Much of the region's vegetation consists of grasses, saltbush, and mulga, a slow-growing evergreen tree capable of surviving in dry conditions. Wildflowers also emerge periodically, but their abundance can vary dramatically depending on how much rain falls.
paras.zh: 该地区的大部分植被由草、盐灌木和穆尔加组成，穆尔加是一种生长缓慢的常绿乔木，能够在干燥条件下生存。野花也会定期出现，但它们的丰度会根据降雨量的不同而发生巨大变化。

paras.en: Unusually Heavy Rains Trigger a Wildflower Explosion
paras.zh: 异常大雨引发野花绽放

paras.en: The exceptional display in 2026 was made possible by a series of cold fronts that carried much-needed moisture into the region.
paras.zh: 一系列冷锋为该地区带来了急需的水分，使得 2026 年的奇观得以实现。

paras.en: According to Australia's Bureau of Meteorology, June brought above-average rainfall, while August was much wetter than normal. These favorable conditions allowed seeds that had remained inactive in the dry soil to germinate, producing an extraordinary variety of wildflowers across the landscape.
paras.zh: 据澳大利亚气象局称，六月的降雨量高于平均水平，而八月的降雨量则远高于正常水平。这些有利的条件使在干燥土壤中保持不活跃的种子得以发芽，在整个景观中产生了各种各样的野花。

paras.en: The colorful transformation extended into the grounds of a radio astronomy observatory operated by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), Australia's national science agency.
paras.zh: 丰富多彩的改造延伸到了由澳大利亚国家科学机构——联邦科学与工业研究组织（CSIRO）运营的射电天文观测站。

paras.en: Among the flowers were several threatened species, adding ecological significance to the seasonal spectacle. The observatory has helped track these vulnerable plants on land that was previously used for livestock grazing.
paras.zh: 这些花朵中有几种受到威胁的物种，为这一季节性景观增添了生态意义。该观测站帮助追踪了以前用于放牧牲畜的土地上的这些脆弱植物。

paras.en: Where Wildflowers Bloom Beneath Deep-Space Telescopes
paras.zh: 深空望远镜下野花盛开的地方

paras.en: While the flowers created an extraordinary scene on the ground, the observatory's usual work takes place far beyond Earth's atmosphere.
paras.zh: 虽然这些花朵在地面上创造了非凡的景象，但天文台的日常工作却远远超出了地球大气层。

paras.en: Known as Inyarrimanha Ilgari Bundara, the CSIRO Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory is a remote research facility dedicated to studying the universe through radio astronomy. Its antenna arrays detect radio signals from celestial objects, allowing scientists to observe and catalog sources across the southern sky.
paras.zh: CSIRO 默奇森射电天文台被称为 Inyarrimanha Ilgari Bundara，是一个致力于通过射电天文学研究宇宙的远程研究设施。它的天线阵列检测来自天体的无线电信号，使科学家能够观察和记录南部天空的源。

paras.en: The observatory's isolated location is particularly important for this work. It sits within a designated "radio quiet" zone, where communication systems and electronic equipment are restricted to reduce interference with sensitive scientific instruments.
paras.zh: 天文台的偏僻位置对于这项工作尤为重要。它位于指定的“无线电安静”区域内，该区域的通信系统和电子设备受到限制，以减少对敏感科学仪器的干扰。

paras.en: Even relatively weak signals generated by human technology can interfere with radio observations, so limiting these disturbances helps astronomers detect faint emissions traveling across space.
paras.zh: 即使人类技术产生的相对微弱的信号也会干扰无线电观测，因此限制这些干扰有助于天文学家检测穿越太空的微弱发射。

paras.en: Australia's Radio Telescopes Have Helped NASA Explore Space
paras.zh: 澳大利亚的射电望远镜帮助美国宇航局探索太空

paras.en: Australia's radio astronomy facilities have a long history of supporting some of NASA's most important space missions.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚的射电天文学设施在支持美国宇航局一些最重要的太空任务方面有着悠久的历史。

paras.en: The Murriyang radio telescope, located in Parkes, New South Wales, helped track Mariner 2 in 1962. That spacecraft became the first successful planetary science mission, marking a major milestone in the exploration of other worlds.
paras.zh: 位于新南威尔士州帕克斯的穆里扬射电望远镜于 1962 年帮助追踪​​了水手 2 号。该航天器成为第一个成功的行星科学任务，标志着探索其他世界的一个重要里程碑。

paras.en: The telescope also played a significant role during the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969, serving as an important receiving station for communications from the historic mission.
paras.zh: 该望远镜还在 1969 年阿波罗 11 号登月期间发挥了重要作用，作为历史性任务通信的重要接收站。

paras.en: CSIRO additionally manages the Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex, one of three major facilities that make up NASA's worldwide Deep Space Network.
paras.zh: 联邦科学与工业研究组织还管理堪培拉深空通信综合体，这是构成美国宇航局全球深空网络的三大设施之一。

paras.en: This global system maintains communications with spacecraft traveling throughout the solar system and beyond, while also supporting radar measurements and radio astronomy research.
paras.zh: 这个全球系统与穿梭于太阳系内外的航天器保持通信，同时还支持雷达测量和射电天文学研究。

paras.en: Both the Murriyang telescope and the Canberra complex contributed to NASA's Artemis II mission in April 2026, continuing Australia's decades-long involvement in space exploration.
paras.zh: Murriyang 望远镜和堪培拉综合体都为 NASA 2026 年 4 月的阿耳忒弥斯二号任务做出了贡献，延续了澳大利亚数十年来对太空探索的参与。

paras.en: For a brief period in 2026, however, one of Australia's most remote astronomical research regions offered a remarkable spectacle much closer to home. While its telescopes continued scanning the distant universe, unusually generous winter rains brought the surrounding outback to life in a brilliant display of wildflowers.
paras.zh: 然而，在 2026 年的一段短暂时间内，澳大利亚最偏远的天文研究区域之一在离家更近的地方呈现出了惊人的奇观。当它的望远镜继续扫描遥远的宇宙时，异常慷慨的冬雨让周围的内陆地区生机勃勃，绽放出绚丽的野花。

paras.en: Materials provided by NASA Earth Observatory. Original written by Lindsey Doermann. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由 NASA 地球观测站提供。原创作者：林赛·杜尔曼。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice

paras.en: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
paras.zh: 科学家发现了衰老的隐藏驱动因素和一种可以对抗小鼠记忆丧失的简单氨基酸

paras.en: - Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days. Even more surprisingly, supplementing with a simple amino acid called D-serine improved memory and learning, offering a potential new approach to age-related cognitive decline.
paras.zh: - 科学家发现，一种名为 Menin 的蛋白质水平下降可能有助于促进衰老，而在年老小鼠中恢复这种蛋白质水平，可以在短短 30 天内逆转一些与年龄相关的变化。更令人惊讶的是，补充一种名为 D-丝氨酸的简单氨基酸可以改善记忆和学习，为与年龄相关的认知衰退提供一种潜在的新方法。

paras.en: What if some of the changes we associate with aging begin with the loss of a single protein deep inside the brain? Scientists investigating that possibility found that restoring a protein called Menin in older mice improved memory, balance, bone mass, and skin thickness in just 30 days. Even more surprisingly, supplementing the animals with a naturally occurring amino acid improved their learning and memory in only three weeks.
paras.zh: 如果我们与衰老相关的一些变化始于大脑深处单一蛋白质的丢失，该怎么办？研究这种可能性的科学家发现，恢复老年小鼠体内一种名为 Menin 的蛋白质，在短短 30 天内就可以改善记忆力、平衡性、骨量和皮肤厚度。更令人惊讶的是，给动物补充天然氨基酸仅在三周内就改善了它们的学习和记忆能力。

paras.en: The findings, originally published in March 2023 in PLOS Biology, came from researchers led by Lige Leng of Xiamen University in China. Their experiments identified a previously overlooked connection between inflammation, brain chemistry, and aging throughout the body. Although the results were obtained in mice, they raised an intriguing possibility: Some effects of aging may be influenced by biological processes in the brain that scientists could eventually learn to modify.
paras.zh: 该研究结果最初于 2023 年 3 月发表在 PLOS Biology 上，由中国厦门大学冷立格领导的研究人员领导。他们的实验发现了炎症、大脑化学物质和全身衰老之间以前被忽视的联系。尽管这些结果是在小鼠身上获得的，但它们提出了一个有趣的可能性：衰老的某些影响可能受到大脑中生物过程的影响，而科学家最终可以学会修改这些生物过程。

paras.en: Research published since then has added evidence that the brain plays an important role in regulating aging. It has also revealed why the seemingly simple supplement findings deserve careful interpretation.
paras.zh: 此后发表的研究进一步证明大脑在调节衰老方面发挥着重要作用。它还揭示了为什么看似简单的补充剂研究结果值得仔细解释。

paras.en: How a Hidden Brain Protein May Influence Aging
paras.zh: 隐藏的大脑蛋白质如何影响衰老

paras.en: At the center of the discovery is the hypothalamus, a small but powerful region near the base of the brain. It helps regulate essential functions such as body temperature, hunger, metabolism, sleep, and hormone production. Because these systems affect nearly every organ, changes in the hypothalamus can have consequences throughout the body.
paras.zh: 这一发现的核心是下丘脑，这是一个靠近大脑底部的小而强大的区域。它有助于调节体温、饥饿、新陈代谢、睡眠和激素产生等基本功能。由于这些系统几乎影响每个器官，因此下丘脑的变化会对整个身体产生影响。

paras.en: Scientists have increasingly recognized the hypothalamus as an important player in aging. One possible reason involves neuroinflammation, the brain's inflammatory response. Although inflammation helps protect against infections and injuries, persistent inflammation can interfere with normal cellular function and contribute to age-related deterioration.
paras.zh: 科学家们越来越认识到下丘脑在衰老过程中发挥着重要作用。一个可能的原因涉及神经炎症，即大脑的炎症反应。虽然炎症有助于防止感染和损伤，但持续的炎症会干扰正常的细胞功能，并导致与年龄相关的恶化。

paras.en: Earlier work by Leng and colleagues had identified Menin as a protein that helps restrain inflammation in the hypothalamus. Menin also participates in regulating gene activity, allowing it to influence multiple biological pathways.
paras.zh: Leng 和同事的早期研究发现 Menin 是一种有助于抑制下丘脑炎症的蛋白质。 Menin 还参与调节基因活性，使其能够影响多种生物途径。

paras.en: The researchers wanted to understand what happens when this protective protein begins to disappear with age.
paras.zh: 研究人员想了解当这种保护性蛋白质随着年龄的增长开始消失时会发生什么。

paras.en: They discovered that Menin levels gradually declined in certain hypothalamic neurons as mice grew older. Interestingly, the same decrease was not observed in astrocytes or microglia, two other important types of brain cells involved in supporting neurons and managing immune responses.
paras.zh: 他们发现，随着小鼠年龄的增长，某些下丘脑神经元中的 Menin 水平逐渐下降。有趣的是，在星形胶质细胞或小胶质细胞（参与支持神经元和管理免疫反应的另外两种重要脑细胞类型）中没有观察到同样的减少。

paras.en: To investigate whether this decline actually contributed to aging, the team developed genetically modified mice in which Menin could be selectively disabled.
paras.zh: 为了调查这种衰退是否真的导致衰老，研究小组开发了转基因小鼠，其中梅宁可以选择性地丧失功能。

paras.en: The results were striking. Mice with reduced Menin activity developed greater inflammation in the hypothalamus, thinner skin, reduced bone mass, and worsening cognitive performance. Their lifespans were also modestly shortened.
paras.zh: 结果是惊人的。 Menin 活性降低的小鼠下丘脑炎症加剧、皮肤变薄、骨量减少以及认知能力恶化。他们的寿命也略有缩短。

paras.en: Rather than simply accompanying aging, the loss of Menin appeared capable of helping drive several of its characteristic changes.
paras.zh: 梅宁的丧失似乎不仅仅伴随着衰老，还有助于推动其一些特征性的变化。

paras.en: Restoring Menin Reversed Several Signs of Aging in 30 Days
paras.zh: 恢复 Menin 在 30 天内逆转了多种衰老迹象

paras.en: The researchers then asked an even more interesting question: If declining Menin contributes to aging, could restoring the protein reverse some of the damage?
paras.zh: 研究人员随后提出了一个更有趣的问题：如果梅宁的减少会导致衰老，那么恢复这种蛋白质是否可以逆转一些损害？

paras.en: To find out, they used a gene delivery technique to increase Menin production in a specific part of the hypothalamus in older (20-month-old) mice. This region, called the ventromedial hypothalamus, helps coordinate metabolism, energy balance, and other bodily functions.
paras.zh: 为了找到答案，他们使用基因传递技术来增加老年（20 个月大）小鼠下丘脑特定部位的 Menin 产量。这个区域被称为下丘脑腹内侧区，有助于协调新陈代谢、能量平衡和其他身体功能。
