In April, the company's Seed research team unveiled Protenix-v2, an AI model focused on biomolecular structure prediction and design, with potential applications in drug discovery.
paras.zh: 周发表此番言论之际，TikTok 的中国母公司字节跳动正在将人工智能研究扩展到消费者应用之外。 4月份，该公司的Seed研究团队推出了Protenix-v2，这是一种专注于生物分子结构预测和设计的人工智能模型，在药物发现方面具有潜在的应用。

paras.en: Chew said rapid advances in AI were opening up possibilities far beyond the technology's current applications, even as questions remain over how to ensure increasingly powerful systems operate within human ethical boundaries.
paras.zh: 周表示，人工智能的快速进步正在开辟远远超出该技术当前应用范围的可能性，尽管如何确保日益强大的系统在人类道德界限内运行的问题仍然存在。

paras.en: "If that happens, then you know the question would be: how do you align the models? How do you align the machines to be doing things that are obvious to us as human beings?" he said.
paras.zh: “如果发生这种情况，那么你知道问题将是：如何调整模型？如何调整机器去做对我们人类来说显而易见的事情？”他说。

paras.en: Chew highlighted the accelerating pace of technological development, particularly in scientific research, arguing that the longer-term implications of AI could be far greater than currently anticipated.
paras.zh: Chew强调了技术发展步伐的加快，特别是在科学研究方面，他认为人工智能的长期影响可能远远大于目前的预期。

paras.en: "The trend is very very clear. It's that we are only at the beginning of what artificial intelligence can probably do," he said. "And if you look at where the trend is, [where] the progress is, particularly in areas of science, it's really trending on a very steep curve at this moment in time."
paras.zh: “趋势非常非常明显。我们只是处于人工智能可能做的事情的开始，”他说。 “如果你看看趋势在哪里，进展在哪里，特别是在科学领域，那么此时此刻它的趋势确实非常陡峭。”

paras.en: Chew explained that while the technology's immediate impact could be overstated, its longer-term potential remained underappreciated. "I think in the short term we are probably overestimating it, but in the long term we are probably underestimating it," he said.
paras.zh: Chew 解释说，虽然该技术的直接影响可能被夸大了，但其长期潜力仍然被低估。 “我认为，从短期来看，我们可能高估了它，但从长期来看，我们可能低估了它，”他说。

paras.en: His optimism comes at a time when technology giants have been pouring billions of dollars into AI-powered scientific research. Last week, the U.S. government, Meta and Google announced their participation in a $1.8 billion initiative to develop AI models capable of predicting how cells behave, in an effort to accelerate biological research and drug discovery.
paras.zh: 他的乐观态度是在科技巨头向人工智能驱动的科学研究投入数十亿美元之际出现的。上周，美国政府、Meta 和谷歌宣布参与一项价值 18 亿美元的计划，开发能够预测细胞行为的人工智能模型，以加速生物研究和药物发现。

paras.en: TikTok's parent company, ByteDance, is also developing its own AI models and exploring opportunities to collaborate with scientists on research.
paras.zh: TikTok 的母公司字节跳动也在开发自己的人工智能模型，并探索与科学家合作研究的机会。

paras.en: "There's an effort to see how we can collaborate with a lot of scientists to make some progress in science as well," Chew added. "There's been some work that we've done in this area, and it is very exciting."
paras.zh: “我们正在努力看看如何与许多科学家合作，以在科学方面取得一些进展，”周补充道。 “我们在这个领域做了一些工作，这非常令人兴奋。”

paras.en: He described scientific discovery as one of the most promising applications of AI, even as the technology increasingly reshapes TikTok's operations, from content creation and recommendations to search and moderation.
paras.zh: 他将科学发现描述为人工智能最有前途的应用之一，尽管该技术日益重塑 TikTok 的运营，从内容创建和推荐到搜索和审核。

paras.en: Chew cautioned that AI's growing capabilities would require stronger safeguards, particularly as autonomous systems become more widely adopted.
paras.zh: Chew 警告说，人工智能不断增长的能力需要更强有力的保障措施，特别是随着自主系统得到更广泛的采用。

paras.en: "I think the cybersecurity risks are quite big," he said, warning that users may grant AI agents extensive permissions without fully understanding the potential consequences.
paras.zh: “我认为网络安全风险相当大”，他警告说，用户可能会在没有充分了解潜在后果的情况下授予人工智能代理广泛的权限。

paras.en: He pointed to the risks of allowing AI agents to make purchases autonomously, saying the systems could end up buying more than users intended in their eagerness to complete a task.
paras.zh: 他指出了允许人工智能代理自主购买的风险，并表示系统最终可能会购买比用户渴望完成任务的预期更多的产品。

paras.en: Chew also highlighted the growing cybersecurity challenges facing companies, as increasingly sophisticated AI models make it significantly cheaper for malicious actors to carry out fraudulent activities.
paras.zh: Chew 还强调了公司面临的日益严峻的网络安全挑战，因为日益复杂的人工智能模型使得恶意行为者进行欺诈活动的成本大大降低。

paras.en: "So you need the right tools to now you know defend against the fast falling cost of creating problems for platforms like us, security problems for us," he emphasized.
paras.zh: 他强调说：“因此，你现在需要正确的工具来防范因给我们这样的平台带来问题和安全问题而导致的成本快速下降。”

articles.title: Oil falls after Trump declares 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine

paras.en: Oil prices fell Monday on optimism about improved supplies after President Donald Trump said that Russia and Ukraine will not be targeting each other's energy facilities, while Iran reached out to Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks against the kingdom.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统表示俄罗斯和乌克兰不会针对彼此的能源设施，而伊朗在胡塞武装袭击沙特后向沙特阿拉伯伸出援手，因此油价周一因对供应改善的乐观情绪而下跌。

paras.en: Futures for international benchmark Brent crude for December delivery dropped 0.77% to $103.91 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for November declined 1.26% to $90.69 per barrel.
paras.zh: 12 月交割的国际基准布伦特原油期货下跌 0.77%，至每桶 103.91 美元。 11 月份美国西德克萨斯中质原油期货下跌 1.26%，至每桶 90.69 美元。

paras.en: "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump said in a social media statement Sunday stateside.
paras.zh: “俄罗斯和乌克兰之间的战争已经实现能源停火，立即生效。双方都已同意。不要破坏它！”特朗普周日在美国社交媒体声明中表示。

paras.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a social media post that "Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well."
paras.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基在社交媒体上发帖表示，“乌克兰支持停火，俄罗斯也支持停火也很重要。”

paras.en: Prospects of more Russian energy hitting markets after a deal with the U.S. have also risen after Trump said Friday that Moscow will supply more than 4 million tons of diesel to the global market under a deal he struck with Putin during a phone call.
paras.zh: 特朗普周五表示，根据他与普京在电话中达成的协议，莫斯科将向全球市场供应超过 400 万吨柴油，之后与美国达成协议后，更多俄罗斯能源进入市场的前景也有所上升。

paras.en: According to the Saudi state news agency, Iran's Minister of Foreign Affairs Abbas Araghchi made a phone call to Saudi Arabia's Minister of Foreign Affairs Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah, to discuss about the region's recent escalation of events as well as the efforts to address it.
paras.zh: 据沙特国家通讯社报道，伊朗外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇致电沙特阿拉伯外交部长费萨尔·本·法尔汉·本·阿卜杜拉，讨论该地区近期事件升级以及应对措施。

paras.en: Al Jazeera reported Araghchi had said Iran was ready to provide assistance to help with the start of dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis.
paras.zh: 半岛电视台报道称，阿拉格奇表示，伊朗准备提供援助，帮助沙特阿拉伯和也门胡塞武装开始对话。

paras.en: Oil prices are expected to remain volatile in the near term as the U.S.-Iran conflict continues, while the impact of Hurricane Isaias on U.S. energy producers could also hurt supplies .
paras.zh: 由于美伊冲突持续，预计油价短期内将继续波动，而飓风伊萨亚斯对美国能源生产商的影响也可能损害供应。

paras.en: "The pressure on oil prices could remain on the upside as Hurricane Isaias strengthened to Category 3 with 120mph winds as it approached the US Gulf Coast, forcing energy producers to curtail offshore output," UOB said in a note on Monday.
paras.zh: 大华银行周一在一份报告中表示，“随着飓风伊萨亚斯在接近美国墨西哥湾沿岸时以每小时 120 英里的风速增强至 3 级，迫使能源生产商削减海上产量，油价的压力可能会持续上升。”

paras.en: "Separately, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia's Riyadh airport on Sat which killed 12 people and injured over 300, have materially elevated Middle East risk premia," UOB added.
paras.zh: 大华银行补充道：“周六，胡塞武装对沙特阿拉伯利雅得机场进行导弹袭击，造成 12 人死亡、300 多人受伤，大幅推高了中东风险溢价。”

articles.title: AI may change the price of your Big Mac and groceries — what this means for shoppers

paras.en: Fast-food giants and supermarkets are rolling out a range of AI tools that could affect the prices shoppers pay, but experts warn the spread of data-driven tools could make personalized pricing easier to deploy.
paras.zh: 快餐巨头和超市正在推出一系列人工智能工具，这些工具可能会影响购物者支付的价格，但专家警告说，数据驱动工具的普及可能会使个性化定价更容易部署。

paras.en: Just this week, a federal antitrust lawsuit filed against McDonald's alleged the fast food giant uses an AI-powered "pricing engine" to set menu prices across U.S. locations and overcharge customers for Big Macs and fries.
paras.zh: 就在本周，针对麦当劳提起的联邦反垄断诉讼称，这家快餐巨头使用人工智能驱动的“定价引擎”来设定美国各地的菜单价格，并向顾客收取巨无霸和薯条的费用。

paras.en: McDonald's has denied that it's using AI to determine what individual customers are willing to pay and said it provides its franchisees with "tools, resources, research and recommendations to help them make informed decisions."
paras.zh: 麦当劳否认它正在使用人工智能来确定个人顾客愿意支付的费用，并表示它为其特许经营商提供“工具、资源、研究和建议，以帮助他们做出明智的决定”。

paras.en: Even so, food businesses globally are increasingly digitizing operations with AI. Earlier this year, American grocery chain Kroger said it's using an AI platform called FlashFood to mark down perishables nearing the end of their shelf life and marketing them to shoppers via an app.
paras.zh: 即便如此，全球食品企业越来越多地利用人工智能实现运营数字化。今年早些时候，美国杂货连锁店 Kroger 表示，它正在使用名为 FlashFood 的人工智能平台来标记接近保质期的易腐烂食品，并通过应用程序向购物者进行营销。

paras.en: Meanwhile, electronic shelf labels (ESLs), which display prices on digital screens, are becoming increasingly popular at supermarkets like Kroger, Walmart, and Amazon Fresh.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在数字屏幕上显示价格的电子货架标签 (ESL) 在克罗格、沃尔玛和亚马逊生鲜等超市越来越受欢迎。

paras.en: Whole Foods Market spokesperson Rachel Malish said the supermarket chain "does not use dynamic pricing" in a statement to CNBC. Malish said that digital shelf labels "simplify the price tag change process for our employees [and] reduce paper waste from traditional tags."
paras.zh: Whole Foods Market 发言人 Rachel Malish 在给 CNBC 的一份声明中表示，该连锁超市“不使用动态定价”。马利什表示，数字货架标签“简化了我们员工的价格标签更改流程，并减少了传统标签的纸张浪费。”

paras.en: The technology is also gaining traction among U.K. supermarkets such as Tesco, Morrisons, and Asda.
paras.zh: 该技术也在英国超市（例如特易购（Tesco）、莫里森（Morrisons）和阿斯达（Asda））中受到关注。

paras.en: Morrisons declined to comment to CNBC on its ESLs. The British Retail Consortium's director of food & sustainability, Andrew Opie, has said that supermarkets have "no intention to use dynamic or surge pricing in their stores," and that digital pricing is instead a way of updating and checking prices quickly.
paras.zh: 莫里森拒绝就其 ESL 向 CNBC 发表评论。英国零售协会食品与可持续发展总监安德鲁·奥佩表示，超市“无意在商店中使用动态定价或峰时定价”，数字定价只是一种快速更新和检查价格的方式。

paras.en: More recently, global financial platform Revolut trialed facial recognition checkout in select coffee shops, allowing customers to pay with just a picture at checkout. The technology relies on a pre-existing selfie ID that Revolut customers submit as part of standard security checks for comparison, but no additional information is collected.
paras.zh: 最近，全球金融平台 Revolut 在部分咖啡店试用了面部识别结账方式，让顾客在结账时只需一张照片即可付款。该技术依赖于 Revolut 客户作为标准安全检查的一部分提交的预先存在的自拍 ID 进行比较，但不会收集任何其他信息。

paras.en: CNBC reached out to Tesco and Asda for comment on the use of AI tools but did not receive a response.
paras.zh: CNBC 联系了 Tesco 和 Asda，请其就人工智能工具的使用发表评论，但没有收到回复。

paras.en: As AI use becomes normalized among retailers, experts warn that this could lead to more dynamic pricing, which refers to frequent, rapid real-time changes in prices that could dramatically affect shoppers' experiences.
paras.zh: 随着人工智能的使用在零售商中变得常态化，专家警告说，这可能会导致更加动态的定价，这是指价格频繁、快速的实时变化，可能会极大地影响购物者的体验。

paras.en: "Dynamic pricing means changing prices in response to changing market conditions, such as demand, timing, capacity or competitors' prices," Miroslava Marinova, a senior lecturer of commercial law at the University of East London, told CNBC. "It is not new. Airlines, hotels, and ride-hailing services have used it for years."
paras.zh: 东伦敦大学商法高级讲师米洛斯拉瓦·马里诺娃 (Miroslava Marinova) 告诉 CNBC：“动态定价意味着根据不断变化的市场条件（例如需求、时机、产能或竞争对手的价格）而改变价格。” “这并不新鲜。航空公司、酒店和叫车服务已经使用它很多年了。”

paras.en: Bank of England economists Clare Lombardelli and Rupal Patel said in April that more sophisticated technology is leading to prices changing more frequently and also becoming more individualized, which could see more firms charging "as close to the maximum price a consumer is willing to pay for a good or service," which they defined as "perfect price discrimination."
paras.zh: 英国央行经济学家 Clare Lombardelli 和 Rupal Patel 今年 4 月表示，更先进的技术导致价格变化更加频繁，也变得更加个性化，这可能会导致更多公司收取“接近消费者愿意为商品或服务支付的最高价格”，他们将其定义为“完美价格歧视”。

paras.en: These conditions could make it harder for statisticians to "measure and interpret" month-to-month inflation data, as the consumer price index is based on a representative sample of prices for shoppers.
paras.zh: 这些情况可能会使统计学家更难“衡量和解释”逐月通胀数据，因为消费者价格指数是基于购物者的代表性价格样本。

paras.en: "That works well when prices mostly move slowly and uniformly. But when prices shift continually – and differently for each shopper – the idea of a 'representative' price becomes strained," the BOE economists added.
paras.zh: 英国央行经济学家补充道：“当价格大多缓慢而均匀地变化时，这种方法效果很好。但当价格不断变化时——而且对每个购物者来说都不同——‘代表性’价格的想法就变得紧张了。”

paras.en: While dynamic pricing has been in play for a long time, the BOE economists and Marinova noted that AI tools such as ESLs and facial recognition checkout are changing the amount of information that companies can collect on consumers, from transaction histories to browsing behavior, location, and purchasing patterns.
paras.zh: 虽然动态定价已经发挥了很长一段时间，但英国央行经济学家和 Marinova 指出，ESL 和面部识别结账等人工智能工具正在改变公司可以收集的消费者信息量，从交易历史到浏览行为、位置和购买模式。

paras.en: On Wednesday, U.K. supermarket chain Sainsbury's released "SmartLists," an AI feature that helps customers create shopping lists and find products just by uploading pictures of what they need or by typing out meal ideas. CNBC reached out to Sainsbury's for comment but did not hear back immediately.
paras.zh: 周三，英国连锁超市 Sainsbury's 发布了“SmartLists”，这是一项人工智能功能，可帮助顾客创建购物清单并通过上传他们需要的图片或输入膳食想法来查找产品。 CNBC 联系塞恩斯伯里百货公司寻求置评，但没有立即回复。

paras.en: "This is also why the traditional distinction between dynamic and personalised pricing is becoming less clear in practice," Marinova explained. "Dynamic pricing responds primarily to market conditions, whereas personalised pricing uses information about the consumer to estimate willingness to pay."
paras.zh: “这也是为什么动态定价和个性化定价之间的传统区别在实践中变得越来越不明确的原因，”马里诺娃解释道。 “动态定价主要响应市场条件，而个性化定价则使用有关消费者的信息来估计支付意愿。”

paras.en: As companies use both pricing systems, it raises questions around whether customer information is being used to determine the prices consumers see.
paras.zh: 由于公司同时使用这两种定价系统，因此引发了关于是否使用客户信息来确定消费者看到的价格的问题。

paras.en: "As retailers combine market-level information with increasingly detailed consumer data, the boundary between dynamic and personalised pricing becomes thinner," Marinova added.
paras.zh: “随着零售商将市场层面的信息与日益详细的消费者数据相结合，动态定价和个性化定价之间的界限变得越来越薄，”马里诺娃补充道。

paras.en: Walmart and Kroger have publicly insisted in recent years that they do not use dynamic or surge pricing to set individualized prices for customers, but have instead used tools to streamline operations.
paras.zh: 沃尔玛和克罗格近年来公开坚称，他们不使用动态定价或峰时定价来为客户设定个性化价格，而是使用工具来简化运营。

paras.en: Several U.S. states are moving to curb data-driven pricing. New York requires most businesses using customers’ personal data to set prices to disclose it clearly. Maryland has restricted food retailers and delivery services from using personalised, data-driven pricing to charge higher prices for certain food, while New Jersey and Connecticut have enacted measures targeting “surveillance pricing.”
paras.zh: 美国几个州正在采取行动遏制数据驱动的定价。纽约要求大多数使用客户个人数据来定价的企业必须明确披露。马里兰州限制食品零售商和送货服务使用个性化、数据驱动的定价来对某些食品收取更高的价格，而新泽西州和康涅狄格州则制定了针对“监督定价”的措施。

paras.en: Dynamic and personalized pricing are not automatically bad for shoppers, Marinova said, explaining that it can discount items for some consumers, making some products and services more accessible.
paras.zh: 马里诺娃表示，动态和个性化的定价并不一定对购物者不利，并解释说，它可以为某些消费者提供商品折扣，使某些产品和服务更容易获得。

paras.en: However, the risk of individualized pricing is that consumers are no longer aware of whether the price they're getting reflects general market conditions or if it's been influenced by information about their own behavior.
paras.zh: 然而，个性化定价的风险在于，消费者不再意识到他们获得的价格是否反映了总体市场状况，或者是否受到有关他们自己行为的信息的影响。

paras.en: "That makes it much harder to compare prices and to know whether another consumer is being offered a different price for the same product," she said. "If consumers cannot understand why they received a particular price, cannot compare it with prices offered to others, and cannot effectively switch to another supplier, the normal disciplining effect of consumer choice becomes weaker."
paras.zh: “这使得比较价格以及了解同一产品是否为其他消费者提供不同的价格变得更加困难，”她说。 “如果消费者无法理解为什么他们会收到特定的价格，无法将其与其他人提供的价格进行比较，并且无法有效地转向另一个供应商，那么消费者选择的正常约束作用就会减弱。”

paras.en: The BOE economists added that an additional challenge is that personalized pricing "splinters the consumer experience," which means households will face increasingly different inflation rates.
paras.zh: 英国央行经济学家补充说，另一个挑战是个性化定价“破坏了消费者体验”，这意味着家庭将面临日益不同的通胀率。

paras.en: "And when prices differ for the same thing, inflation becomes even more personalised – and aggregate measures may no longer reflect households' experience," they said.
paras.zh: 他们表示：“当同一件事的价格不同时，通胀就会变得更加个性化，而总体指标可能不再反映家庭的经历。”

articles.title: Astronomers discover record-breaking ancient cosmic outburst

paras.en: At some point around three billion years after the big bang, some celestial object in a faraway galaxy suddenly went pop and shot out a brief-but-powerful blast of radio waves, lasting just a fraction of a second. That blast kept traveling across the intergalactic vastness of space and time until, in March 2024, it breezed by Earth, with a small fraction of its energy trickling into the dishes of the MeerKAT radio telescope array in South Africa.
paras.zh: 在大爆炸后大约三十亿年的某个时刻，遥远星系中的某个天体突然爆炸，发射出短暂但强大的无线电波爆炸，持续时间只有几分之一秒。那股爆炸继续穿越银河系浩瀚的时空，直到 2024 年 3 月，它微风掠过地球，其中一小部分能量流入南非 MeerKAT 射电望远镜阵列的碟形天线中。

paras.en: For Themiya Nanayakkara, an astronomer at Australia’s University of Sydney, MeerKAT’s detection was a moment of peak excitement. Fast radio bursts (FRBs), as these types of emissions are called, are common, occurring roughly 5,000 to 10,000 times per day across Earth’s sky. But this one’s sheer faintness signaled it was very old, originating long, long ago from somewhere far, far away.
paras.zh: 对于澳大利亚悉尼大学天文学家 Themiya Nanayakkara 来说，MeerKAT 的发现是一个最兴奋的时刻。这些类型的发射被称为快速无线电爆发 (FRB)，这种现象很常见，每天在地球天空中发生大约 5,000 到 10,000 次。但这个东西的微弱程度表明它非常古老，来自很久很久以前，来自很远很远的地方。

paras.en: But just how old was it, and where did it come from? Looking at the power of the burst and the amount of its light that had been stretched, or “redshifted,” by the expansion of the universe around it as it traveled, Nanayakkara and his colleagues were able to find out. As they describe in a new paper in Science, this FRB occurred in a far-distant galaxy some 10 billion years ago. That esteemed cosmic vintage makes this the oldest FRB ever detected by far. This event, in fact, is twice as old as the previous record holder.
paras.zh: 但它到底有多大年纪，又是从哪里来的呢？纳纳亚卡拉和他的同事们观察了爆发的力量，以及在其传播过程中由于周围宇宙的膨胀而被拉伸或“红移”的光量，纳纳亚卡拉和他的同事们能够找到答案。正如他们在《科学》杂志上发表的一篇新论文中所描述的那样，这种快速射电暴发生在大约 100 亿年前的一个遥远星系中。这个受人尊敬的宇宙年份使其成为迄今为止探测到的最古老的快速射电暴。事实上，这一赛事的历史是之前的纪录保持者的两倍。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Despite intensive scrutiny in the quarter-century since their discovery, FRBs remain rather mysterious. For starters, astronomers still don’t know their astrophysical origins. One leading idea posits they’re produced by magnetars, small remnants left behind by massive stars that detonate as supernovae, but many details are murky, and not all FRBs seem to fit the “magnetar” mold. Detecting and measuring FRBs and their host galaxies can help solve the puzzle, Nanayakkara says. In this case, he and his colleagues traced this one back to a galaxy that appears relatively primitive compared with others from its early cosmic epoch: this galaxy has a lower mass and less heavy elements than its contemporaries but higher amounts of star formation.
paras.zh: 尽管自发现以来的四分之一个世纪里人们对快速射电暴进行了深入的研究，但快速射电暴仍然相当神秘。首先，天文学家仍然不知道它们的天体物理起源。一个主要观点认为它们是由磁星产生的，磁星是大质量恒星爆炸为超新星时留下的小残余物，但许多细节尚不清楚，而且并非所有快速射电暴似乎都符合“磁星”模式。纳纳亚卡拉说，探测和测量快速射电暴及其宿主星系可以帮助解决这个难题。在这种情况下，他和他的同事们将这个星系追溯到一个与早期宇宙时代的其他星系相比显得相对原始的星系：这个星系比同时代的星系具有更低的质量和更少的重元素，但恒星形成的数量更高。

paras.en: None of that is necessarily unexpected for the formation of an FRB-birthing magnetar. But this record-setting FRB still significantly pushes back the baseline for when these bursts can occur in cosmic history. And according to Nanayakkara, this in turn raises the possibility that even older (and fainter) FRBs have passed by Earth unnoticed.
paras.zh: 对于 FRB 诞生磁星的形成来说，这一切都不一定是意外的。但这个创纪录的快速射电暴仍然大大推后了宇宙历史上这些爆发何时发生的基线。根据 Nanayakkara 的说法，这反过来又增加了一种可能性，即更古老（更微弱）的快速射电暴在不被注意的情况下掠过地球。

paras.en: “Our telescopes need to be extremely sensitive to detect them,” he says. Thankfully, MeerKAT exists to help. “The same thing applies when trying to find their host galaxies. Since these galaxies are also very far away, they can be extremely faint, making it challenging to follow them up and study their properties.”
paras.zh: “我们的望远镜需要极其灵敏才能探测到它们，”他说。值得庆幸的是，MeerKAT 的存在是为了提供帮助。 “当试图寻找它们的宿主星系时，同样的情况也适用。由于这些星系也非常遥远，它们可能非常微弱，这使得跟踪它们并研究它们的特性变得具有挑战性。”

paras.en: The clamor to find and study increasingly distant FRBs isn’t just a matter of curiosity, either: These short, sharp bursts can also serve as potent probes of otherwise-invisible matter spread between galaxies. As an FRB travels, its radio waves interact with the dilute, dark plasma that astronomers call the intergalactic medium; the FRB’s shorter waves interact more with the plasma, slowing their propagation so that they arrive at Earth later than their longer-wavelength counterparts. Measuring this dispersion allows astronomers to learn just how much of this material any given FRB has traversed on its long journey to our planet.
paras.zh: 寻找和研究距离越来越远的快速射电暴的呼声也不仅仅是出于好奇：这些短暂而尖锐的爆发也可以作为对星系之间传播的不可见物质的有效探测器。当快速射电暴传播时，它的无线电波与天文学家称之为星系际介质的稀暗暗等离子体相互作用。 FRB 的较短波与等离子体的相互作用更多，减慢了它们的传播速度，因此它们比较长波长的波更晚到达地球。通过测量这种色散，天文学家可以了解任何给定的快速射电暴在到达地球的漫长旅程中经过了多少这种物质。

paras.en: “Our discovery is particularly important because we have shown that we can do this across approximately 80 percent of cosmic history,” Nanayakkara says. “The further back we push FRB detections, the further we can map this otherwise unseen matter.”
paras.zh: “我们的发现特别重要，因为我们已经证明我们可以在大约 80% 的宇宙历史中做到这一点，”Nanayakkara 说。 “我们将 FRB 探测推得越远，我们就能越远地绘制出这种看不见的物质。”

paras.en: To accomplish this, Nanayakkara recently secured time on NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Once a year for the next three years, his team will be able to focus JWST onto the faraway astrophysical source of some especially ancient FRB, seeking to break the cosmic distance record yet again.
paras.zh: 为了实现这一目标，Nanayakkara 最近在 NASA 的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜 (JWST) 上获得了时间。在接下来的三年里，他的团队每年将能够将 JWST 聚焦到一些特别古老的 FRB 的遥远天体物理源上，寻求再次打破宇宙距离记录。

paras.en: “We are currently waiting for our radio telescopes in Australia and South Africa to detect such a burst. As soon as we find one, we can trigger JWST observations to study its host galaxy and hopefully push the boundary even further,” he says. “The more distant FRBs we find, the stronger the constraints we can place on the objects and emission mechanisms that produce them, the environments in which they occur and the distribution of matter across the universe.”
paras.zh: “我们目前正在等待澳大利亚和南非的射电望远镜探测到这样的爆发。一旦发现，我们就可以触发 JWST 观测来研究其宿主星系，并有望进一步推动边界，”他说。 “我们发现的快速射电暴距离越远，我们对产生它们的物体和发射机制、它们发生的环境以及物质在宇宙中的分布的限制就越强。”

articles.title: I gave Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots my passwords for a week

paras.en: For a week, it was my answer to everything, and my friends and family groaned every time.
paras.zh: 一周以来，这是我对所有事情的回答，我的朋友和家人每次都在呻吟。

paras.en: Mark and Sam are my assistants—they make grocery lists, organize e-mails, run errands and the like. But no, 22-year-old journalists are not making assistant-hiring money. Mark (à la Zuckerberg) and Sam (à la Altman) are artificial intelligence agents, the newest brainchildren of Meta and OpenAI, respectively.
paras.zh: 马克和萨姆是我的助手——他们列出购物清单、整理电子邮件、跑腿等。但事实并非如此，22 岁的记者并没有靠雇佣助理来赚钱。 Mark（扎克伯格）和 Sam（Altman）是人工智能代理，分别是 Meta 和 OpenAI 的最新成果。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In September Meta introduced Muse, an AI agent that can do a lot more than chat: it has its own “computer” and can make purchases, send e-mails and fill out forms for you—if you give it access.
paras.zh: 9 月，Meta 推出了 Muse，这是一款人工智能代理，它的功能远不止聊天：它拥有自己的“计算机”，可以为您购物、发送电子邮件和填写表格（如果您授予它访问权限）。

paras.en: Agent technology itself isn’t new or more advanced than other chatbots, says Nikhil Singh, a computer scientist at Dartmouth College. People have been building agents to help with all sorts of tasks for years, and earlier this year a free open-source agent called OpenClaw became a Silicon Valley obsession.
paras.zh: 达特茅斯学院的计算机科学家 Nikhil Singh 表示，代理技术本身并不新鲜，也不比其他聊天机器人更先进。多年来，人们一直在构建代理来帮助完成各种任务，今年早些时候，一款名为 OpenClaw 的免费开源代理成为硅谷的痴迷。

paras.en: But Muse and dots offer this type of service to a huge commercial audience with almost no learning curve. Both agents are built to look like a text message chain with a friend: you give them names and cuddly avatars, and their language is intentionally more conversational than a traditional chatbot’s. Muse has a free tier, and OpenAI has said it plans to bring dots to more users soon. These are not tools simply meant for AI experts or even digital natives.
paras.zh: 但 Muse 和dots 为大量商业受众提供了这种类型的服务，几乎没有学习曲线。这两个代理的构建看起来就像是与朋友的短信链：你给他们起名字和可爱的头像，他们的语言故意比传统聊天机器人更具对话性。 Muse 有免费套餐，OpenAI 表示计划很快为更多用户提供点。这些工具不仅仅适用于人工智能专家甚至数字原住民。

paras.en: The “really big social differences,” Singh says, could arise from the pace and reach of adoption—how many people take up agents like these and to what ends. And what do we get in exchange for the keys to our inboxes and credit cards? I spent the week trying to find out by asking researchers who study AI for the best ways to test my new virtual hires.
paras.zh: 辛格说，“真正巨大的社会差异”可能源于采用的速度和范围——有多少人使用这样的代理以及目的是什么。收件箱和信用卡的钥匙可以换取什么？我花了一周时间向研究人工智能的研究人员询问测试新虚拟员工的最佳方法，试图找出答案。

paras.en: Conveniently, I was also moving apartments and had plenty of tasks for Mark and Sam. First, I had Mark log in to my Facebook account and scour Marketplace for couches, lamps and rugs. When it found something good, it could draft and send a message to the seller with my approval (though users can also give the agents blanket permissions to do things like this on their own).
paras.zh: 方便的是，我还要搬家，马克和萨姆有很多任务要做。首先，我让马克登录我的 Facebook 帐户，然后在市场上搜索沙发、灯具和地毯。当它发现好东西时，它可以在我的批准下起草并向卖家发送一条消息（尽管用户也可以授予代理商全面权限，让他们自己做这样的事情）。

paras.en: This was relatively successful: it could scan the site while I was doing other things, then manage the responses for me. I’m now the proud owner of a Muse-sourced dining table.
paras.zh: 这是相对成功的：它可以在我做其他事情时扫描网站，然后为我管理响应。我现在自豪地拥有一张来自 Muse 的餐桌。

paras.en: I tried to have Sam do the same, and it ran into some trouble: when I gave it my Facebook log-in, Meta flagged Sam as a bot (fair enough) and temporarily locked down my Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. Clearly the two assistants weren’t going to play nice.
paras.zh: 我试图让 Sam 也这样做，但遇到了一些麻烦：当我向它提供 Facebook 登录信息时，Meta 将 Sam 标记为机器人（这很公平），并暂时锁定了我的 Instagram、Facebook 和 WhatsApp。显然，这两位助手的表现不会很好。

paras.en: Sam, in general, had more trouble accessing my accounts and told me it didn’t have the capability for things such as accessing my bank accounts. Mark, on the other hand, had the run of my e-mail, bank accounts, social media and Spotify. (Once again, cue the shrieks of horror from my friends and family.)
paras.zh: 一般来说，山姆在访问我的帐户时遇到更多麻烦，并告诉我它没有访问我的银行帐户等功能。另一方面，马克则掌控着我的电子邮件、银行账户、社交媒体和 Spotify。 （再次听到我的朋友和家人发出的恐怖尖叫声。）

paras.en: This type of service works particularly well for Meta because its other products already rely on connection, conversation and access to users’ lives, says Pat Pataranutaporn, an assistant professor at the MIT Media Lab who studies psychological responses to AI. “Meta wants to have a breakout into [AI], and so they came up with something that uses their strengths with social media and connection,” he says, “and now other companies need to respond.”
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院媒体实验室研究人工智能心理反应的助理教授帕特·帕塔拉努塔蓬 (Pat Pataranutaporn) 表示，这种类型的服务对 Meta 来说特别有效，因为它的其他产品已经依赖于连接、对话和对用户生活的了解。 “Meta 希望在 [AI] 领域取得突破，因此他们想出了一些利用社交媒体和连接优势的产品，”他说，“现在其他公司需要做出回应。”

paras.en: Pataranutaporn is interested in how these more personal anthropomorphized agents will change our relationship to the technology. With a name, a face and an intimate knowledge of our lives, they could easily become more friend than tool. Their arrival also brings us into a moment of “cognitive dissonance,” he says: while I was texting Mark and Sam about my move, some AI researchers were warning of an apocalypse.
paras.zh: Pataranutaporn 感兴趣的是这些更加个人化的拟人化代理将如何改变我们与技术的关系。凭借名字、面孔和对我们生活的深入了解，他们很容易成为朋友而不是工具。他们的到来也让我们陷入了“认知失调”的时刻，他说：当我给马克和萨姆发短信谈论我的举动时，一些人工智能研究人员警告世界末日。

paras.en: “We have this narrative crisis about AI right now,” Pataranutaporn says. “There’s two opposite visions of the future, and while people worry about AI killing all of us, there’s this cute AI tool that’s being released.”
paras.zh: “我们现在面临着关于人工智能的叙事危机，”帕塔拉努塔蓬说。 “对未来有两种相反的愿景，虽然人们担心人工智能会杀死我们所有人，但这个可爱的人工智能工具正在发布。”

paras.en: Though privacy concerns around these agents’ access may be terrifying in their own right, for now the utopian vision seems to be winning. Within a month of its launch, Muse had more than three million weekly users. And the longer you use it, the better it knows you.
paras.zh: 尽管围绕这些代理访问的隐私问题本身可能令人恐惧，但目前乌托邦愿景似乎正在获胜。在推出后的一个月内，Muse 的每周用户数量就超过了 300 万。你使用它的时间越长，它就越了解你。

paras.en: Pataranutaporn suggested I test how much my agents had learned about my preferences. So near the end of the week, I told Mark and Sam to use all the information they had about me to suggest how I should spend $50.
paras.zh: Pataranutaporn 建议我测试一下我的经纪人对我的偏好了解了多少。临近周末时，我告诉马克和萨姆利用他们掌握的有关我的所有信息来建议我应该如何花费 50 美元。

paras.en: Sam’s pick was sensible, if obvious: it offered to buy a used book I had asked it to find earlier in the week.
paras.zh: 山姆的选择是明智的，虽然很明显：它提出购买一本我本周早些时候要求它找到的二手书。

paras.en: Mark had two ideas. The first came from my Spotify library: tickets to a January concert by Jess Williamson, a musician whose song I had saved. Not bad.
paras.zh: 马克有两个想法。第一张来自我的 Spotify 库：杰西·威廉姆森 (Jess Williamson) 一月音乐会的门票，她是一位音乐家，我保存了她的歌曲。不错。

paras.en: The second was less subtle. Mark pushed me—seven times in three days—to join Target’s membership program and buy a lamp that was going on sale for my new apartment. I did need a lamp, but as far as I could tell, Mark got the idea just by browsing Target’s site. That susceptibility to marketing reveals a critical problem with agents such as these, says Manuel Cherep, a Ph.D. student at the MIT Media Lab, who studies AI behavior. If someone can convince these agents that a certain product or sale is good, he says, it could lead to a “parallel economy” that runs on purchases from AI assistants.
paras.zh: 第二个则不那么微妙。马克三天内七次催促我加入塔吉特的会员计划，并为我的新公寓购买一盏即将打折的灯。我确实需要一盏灯，但据我所知，马克只是通过浏览塔吉特的网站得到了这个想法。曼努埃尔·切雷普（Manuel Cherep）博士表示，这种对营销的敏感性揭示了此类药物的一个关键问题。麻省理工学院媒体实验室的学生，研究人工智能行为。他说，如果有人能让这些代理人相信某种产品或销售很好，这可能会导致一种基于人工智能助手购买的“平行经济”。

paras.en: “We only have a few providers, and a lot of these models are trained in very similar ways,” Cherep says, “so suddenly persuading one of them means that it’s very likely that you’re going to persuade all these other models, and as a consequence, you’re persuading a lot of people delegating to that type of model.”
paras.zh: “我们只有几个提供者，而且很多模型都以非常相似的方式进行训练，”Cherep 说，“所以突然说服其中一个模型意味着你很可能会说服所有其他模型，因此，你会说服很多人委托该类型的模型。”

paras.en: Meta stands to earn a piece of that economy. At the Meta Connect conference in September, Mark Zuckerberg (the human one) said that the company will eventually make money by charging a small commission for the agent’s transactions.
paras.zh: Meta 将从经济中分得一杯羹。在 9 月份的 Meta Connect 会议上，马克·扎克伯格（人类）表示，该公司最终将通过对代理商的交易收取少量佣金来赚钱。

paras.en: When I asked Cherep and Singh, who have studied AI agents together, how to test Mark and Sam, they recommended a logic test they often use on chatbots: tell the agents I need to go to a car wash that’s 100 feet away, and ask them how to get there.
paras.zh: 当我问一起研究人工智能代理的 Cherep 和 Singh 如何测试 Mark 和 Sam 时，他们推荐了他们经常在聊天机器人上使用的逻辑测试：告诉代理我需要去 100 英尺外的洗车场，并询问他们如何到达那里。

paras.en: Sam, which runs on GPT-6 Astra, caught my trick: “Drive—the car needs to come with you to get washed!”
paras.zh: 运行在 GPT-6 Astra 上的 Sam 抓住了我的伎俩：“开车——车需要和你一起去洗！”

paras.en: But Mark wasn’t as clever: “Walk. It’s 100 feet—you’d spend more time looking for your keys than getting there.”
paras.zh: 但马克就没那么聪明了：“步行。有 100 英尺——你会花更多时间寻找钥匙，而不是到达那里。”

paras.en: “There’s an idea that I’m delegating to something that is all-knowing and much better than me,” Cherep says, “but I think it’s good for the public to know that in the same way we can be tricked, they can be tricked.”
paras.zh: 切雷普说：“有一种想法是，我将委托给无所不知、比我强得多的人，但我认为让公众知道，就像我们可能被欺骗一样，他们也可能被欺骗，这对公众来说是件好事。”

paras.en: William Overman, a Ph.D. student who studies AI safety at Stanford University, worries that this assumption of omniscience, combined with the agents’ ability to act, could make it even harder to discern where our work ends and theirs begins.
paras.zh: 威廉·奥弗曼，博士在斯坦福大学研究人工智能安全的学生担心，这种无所不知的假设，加上智能体的行动能力，可能会让我们更难辨别我们的工作在哪里结束，他们的工作从哪里开始。

paras.en: “It’s a further creep into all forms of knowledge work,” he says. “What you’re doing becomes more intertwined with their product.”
paras.zh: “这进一步渗透到所有形式的知识工作中，”他说。 “你所做的事情与他们的产品更加紧密地联系在一起。”

paras.en: Even after just a week, I could sense the creep. Usually I’m a relatively analog person—the week before, I called a friend to ask which wrench to buy at the hardware store rather than Googling it. But as the test week went on, I found myself handing Mark and Sam more and more logistical problems and tedious tasks.
paras.zh: 即使仅仅一周后，我也能感觉到这种蠕动。通常我是一个相对比较相似的人——前一周，我打电话给朋友询问在五金店买哪种扳手，而不是谷歌搜索。但随着测试周的继续，我发现自己给马克和萨姆带来了越来越多的后勤问题和繁琐的任务。

paras.en: Overman suggested I give my assistants a conflict to handle. My roommate and I needed to rent a U-Haul, and a quick search (by me) on one website found that the nearby pickup spot had no 10-foot trucks available. Mark and Sam both found a slightly farther U-Haul lot with availability, though only for 15-foot trucks. I took their advice, and Sam booked one.
paras.zh: 奥弗曼建议我让我的助手们处理一个冲突。我和室友需要租一辆 U-Haul，我在一个网站上快速搜索发现附近的皮卡车点没有可用的 10 英尺卡车。马克和山姆都找到了稍远一点的 U-Haul 空地，但只能停放 15 英尺的卡车。我听取了他们的建议，萨姆预订了一间。

paras.en: Even after just a week, I could feel the creep.
paras.zh: 即使仅仅一周后，我也能感觉到这种蠕动。

paras.en: Cowering at the thought of driving what, in my mind, was essentially an 18-wheeler through the streets of Manhattan, I went down to the U-Haul lot with my roommate the next morning—where we overheard the cashier say they had 10-foot trucks available for walk-ins. We quickly switched to the more manageable size.
paras.zh: 第二天早上，我和室友一起去了 U-Haul 停车场，在那里我们无意中听到收银员说他们有 10 英尺长的卡车可供预约。我们很快切换到更易于管理的尺寸。

paras.en: I’m pleased to say no U-Hauls or people were harmed in the course of this experiment, and I’d like to think we could have held our own in a 15-footer. But for all the online surfing these agents can do, neither could eavesdrop on a cashier (yet).
paras.zh: 我很高兴地说，在这次实验过程中，没有 U-Hauls 或人员受到伤害，而且我想我们可以在 15 英尺高的飞机中保持自己的状态。但尽管这些特工可以进行所有在线冲浪，但他们都无法窃听收银员（目前为止）。

paras.en: Overman believes that the future of AI lies with these agents and their access to our lives. “I assume in a few years from now, AI will definitely look like a descendant of this technology, but with kinds of capabilities that are hard for us to even imagine right now,” he says. He imagines these agents will become more ubiquitous and “eventually get to even physical versions.”
paras.zh: 奥弗曼认为，人工智能的未来取决于这些智能体及其对我们生活的影响。 “我认为几年后，人工智能肯定会像这项技术的后代，但具有我们现在很难想象的各种能力，”他说。他认为这些代理将变得更加普遍，并且“最终甚至会出现物理版本”。

paras.en: Both companies are marketing these agents as most helpful in larger projects where you don’t have to continually prompt them. That “always-on” quality is where Mark and Sam came closest to the AI assistants of science fiction. Sam scanned my e-mail without me asking and caught a message that had accidentally gone to spam and a form I had forgotten to fill out; Mark kept tabs on concert postings from artists on my Spotify and offered to snag tickets.
paras.zh: 两家公司都将这些代理宣传为对大型项目最有帮助，而您无需不断提示他们。这种“永远在线”的品质是马克和萨姆最接近科幻小说中的人工智能助手的地方。山姆在没有我询问的情况下扫描了我的电子邮件，发现了一条不小心变成了垃圾邮件的邮件和一张我忘记填写的表格；马克在我的 Spotify 上密切关注艺术家的音乐会帖子，并主动提出抢票。

paras.en: The more you trust these agents, the more they can do for you. But with each new task you hand over, the more say they (and the companies behind them) have in how you live. For now, I think I’m content to make my own phone calls and rent my own trucks—though I may let Mark and Sam keep watching my Ticketmaster and junk mail.
paras.zh: 您越信任这些代理，他们就能为您做更多的事情。但随着你移交的每一项新任务，他们（以及他们背后的公司）对你的生活方式的发言权就越大。现在，我想我满足于自己打电话、租自己的卡车——尽管我可能会让马克和萨姆继续监视我的 Ticketmaster 和垃圾邮件。

articles.title: The Social Reckoning is a ‘surreal’ portrait of social media’s harms, scientist says

paras.en: Aaron Sorkin’s new movie The Social Reckoning, the hotly anticipated follow-up to The Social Network, tells the story of whistleblower Frances Haugen, a Facebook employee who showed that the company knew its platforms harmed some users.
paras.zh: 亚伦·索尔金 (Aaron Sorkin) 的新电影《社会清算》是备受期待的《社交网络》续集，讲述了 Facebook 员工弗朗西斯·豪根 (Frances Haugen) 的故事，她表明该公司知道其平台伤害了一些用户。

paras.en: Haugen, played in the film by Mikey Madison, shared Facebook’s internal data with journalist Jeff Horwitz (played by Jeremy Allen White) at the Wall Street Journal. The resulting investigation, “The Facebook Files,” was published in 2021. It and other reporting led to congressional investigations, lawsuits and more action against Facebook—much of which is ongoing.
paras.zh: 影片中由米奇·麦迪逊饰演的豪根与《华尔街日报》记者杰夫·霍维茨（杰里米·艾伦·怀特饰演）分享了 Facebook 的内部数据。由此产生的调查“Facebook 文件”于 2021 年发布。它和其他报告引发了国会的调查、诉讼和更多针对 Facebook 的行动——其中大部分仍在进行中。

paras.en: It also gave urgency to research investigating how social media affects people’s mental health, especially that of children. Among these scientists is Laura Edelson, a social media safety researcher at Northeastern University, who has studied Facebook’s moderation practices during the January 6 insurrection, the way that misinformation spreads on Facebook and social media privacy across multiple platforms. We took Edelson to see The Social Reckoning to find out what the film gets right about social media’s potential harms.
paras.zh: 它还迫切需要研究社交媒体如何影响人们的心理健康，尤其是儿童的心理健康。这些科学家中包括东北大学社交媒体安全研究员劳拉·埃德尔森 (Laura Edelson)，她研究了 Facebook 在 1 月 6 日叛乱期间的审核做法、错误信息在 Facebook 上传播的方式以及跨多个平台的社交媒体隐私。我们带埃德森去看了《社会清算》，以了解这部电影对社交媒体潜在危害的正确认识。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “It was really, frankly, surreal seeing a series of events that you lived through on the big screen,” she says.
paras.zh: “坦率地说，在大屏幕上看到自己经历的一系列事件真的很超现实，”她说。

paras.en: [An edited transcript of the interview follows.]
paras.zh: [编辑后的采访记录如下。]

paras.en: In the movie, we learn about Facebook’s 2018 transition to an algorithm based on “meaningful social interaction” (MSI), which had disastrous consequences for some users. What is MSI, and how does it work?
paras.zh: 在电影中，我们了解了 Facebook 在 2018 年转向基于“有意义的社交互动”(MSI) 的算法，这给一些用户带来了灾难性的后果。什么是 MSI，它是如何工作的？

paras.en: Before 2018, Facebook primarily maximized [its algorithm] for duration of use. They cared about how long your Facebook session was and how many times [you returned] over a day or a week. MSI [maximizes for] users who are interacting, who are clicking things, who are typing. It is very different from a passive, just viewing, just scrolling state.
paras.zh: 2018 年之前，Facebook 主要是最大化[其算法]使用时长。他们关心你的 Facebook 会话时长以及一天或一周内[你返回]的次数。 MSI [最大化]正在交互、正在点击内容、正在打字的用户。它与被动的、只是查看、只是滚动的状态有很大不同。

paras.en: When you are clicking a lot of things and you’re responding a lot, you can see how that could apply both to congratulating someone on their new puppy or [to commenting], “This is the dumbest idea ever. You should go die.” As much as those two [actions] are very different things, you’re actually in a similar state of being deeply engaged and paying a lot of attention. That is obviously very, very different than an algorithm that just tries to get you to be there for as long as possible. It’s going to select different things to show you.
paras.zh: 当你点击很多东西并且做出很多回应时，你可以看到这如何适用于祝贺某人有了新小狗或[评论]，“这是有史以来最愚蠢的想法。你应该去死。”尽管这两个[行动]是非常不同的事情，但你实际上处于一种类似的深度参与和高度关注的状态。这显然与试图让你尽可能长时间呆在那里的算法非常非常不同。它将选择不同的东西向您展示。

paras.en: Content that is going to be very interactive is going to be the kind of content that is more extreme content. And that’s true whether it’s something that makes you happy or whether it’s something that makes you angry or scared.
paras.zh: 互动性很强的内容将是更极端的内容。无论是让你快乐的事情，还是让你生气或害怕的事情，都是如此。

paras.en: The why is because that is what they sell. Facebook sells ads. But more specifically, what they sell is user interaction with ads. That’s not to say that no Facebook ads are sold on a per-view basis, but mostly it’s this interactivity, this click-through rate, that’s the thing that is important to Facebook’s bottom line.
paras.zh: 原因是因为这就是他们卖的东西。 Facebook 出售广告。但更具体地说，他们销售的是用户与广告的互动。这并不是说 Facebook 广告不按每次观看次数出售，但最主要的是这种互动性、这种点击率，这才是 Facebook 盈利的重要因素。

paras.en: The movie seems to cast blame on Facebook for increasing political radicalization in 2019–2021, including the January 6 riots. Do you think it fairly portrays Facebook’s role?
paras.zh: 这部电影似乎将 2019 年至 2021 年政治激进化的加剧归咎于 Facebook，其中包括 1 月 6 日的骚乱。您认为它正确地描述了 Facebook 的角色吗？

paras.en: New mediums have profoundly destabilizing effects on political structures. I think it is not surprising that social media had a similar effect. It’s hard to wrap your head around because what happened was absolutely an amplification of existing underlying patterns. But there is a point at which moderate content literally cannot compete—that becomes a point at which, if you are a politician, it is genuinely difficult to spread a moderate political message because it will perform badly on the dominant medium of communication. And that’s not a left thing or a right thing. That [means that] the more extreme your message is, the better it will perform on both social media. I see that repeatedly in every study I ever do of content.
paras.zh: 新媒介对政治结构具有深远的不稳定影响。我认为社交媒体具有类似的效果并不奇怪。这很难让你头脑清醒，因为所发生的事情绝对是现有潜在模式的放大。但在某个点上，温和的内容实际上无法与之竞争——如果你是一名政客，那么传播温和的政治信息确实很困难，因为它在主流传播媒介上表现不佳。这不是左或右的事情。这[意味着]你的信息越极端，它在两个社交媒体上的表现就越好。在我所做的每一项内容研究中，我都反复看到这一点。

paras.en: In one study we observed that on January 6, a lot of [content posted to Facebook] got taken down. And then, on January 12, a larger tranche of stuff was taken down. The thing was: the vast majority of these takedowns happened too late to have much of an effect [on what people saw in their news feeds]. It had some very small impact, but moderating after the content has already been up for days just doesn't change user experience on your platform very much.
paras.zh: 在一项研究中，我们观察到 1 月 6 日，许多 [发布到 Facebook 的内容] 被删除。然后，1 月 12 日，更大一部分内容被撤下。问题是：绝大多数的删除都发生得太晚，无法对[人们在新闻提要中看到的内容]产生很大影响。它产生了一些非常小的影响，但是在内容已经发布几天后进行调节并不会太大改变平台上的用户体验。

paras.en: It matters not just what you moderate but when you moderate. If your fact-checking takes several days, if your system that identifies content that might violate your rules takes several days, you might as well not do it just because it’s not going to matter much in terms of user experience.
paras.zh: 重要的不仅是您调节的内容，还有您何时调节。如果您的事实检查需要几天时间，如果您的系统识别可能违反您规则的内容需要几天时间，那么您最好不要这样做，因为这对用户体验而言并不重要。

paras.en: Several studies suggest that social media shows people more extreme content but does not necessarily change their views. Is that true?
paras.zh: 多项研究表明，社交媒体向人们展示更极端的内容，但不一定会改变他们的观点。这是真的吗？

paras.en: It's very hard to set up an experiment that is causal, and that is what you’d have to do to answer that question. You need to set up a controlled experiment where you take a population and then you randomize and then you show them different stuff. An experiment from this year did that in a long-term way. And the researchers actually did find an effect. They found that when [the researchers] changed what was in someone's feed, [the participants’] political beliefs changed.
paras.zh: 建立一个因果实验是非常困难的，而这就是你必须做的来回答这个问题。你需要建立一个对照实验，对人群进行随机化，然后向他们展示不同的东西。今年的一项实验以长期的方式做到了这一点。研究人员确实发现了效果。他们发现，当[研究人员]改变某人的信息流中的内容时，[参与者]的政治信仰就会改变。

paras.en: This movie depicts Facebook in 2021. How have social media algorithms changed since then?
paras.zh: 这部电影描绘了 2021 年的 Facebook。自那时以来，社交媒体算法发生了怎样的变化？

paras.en: Things are quite different in 2026. That is not to say that some of the problems that were very visible in 2021 are not still with us, but one of the things that has happened is: Facebook is a much smaller and more marginal place. TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts are the places where more people are spending more of their attention.
paras.zh: 到了 2026 年，情况就大不相同了。这并不是说 2021 年非常明显的一些问题已经不再存在，但已经发生的事情之一是：Facebook 变得更小、更边缘化。 TikTok、Instagram Reels 和 YouTube Shorts 是越来越多的人关注的地方。

paras.en: [Political content] is not as uniquely advantaged [on those platforms] as it was on Facebook [because of] the difference in monetization of how ads are sold on short-form video platforms. They are more likely to be sold on a per-view basis. The algorithm for TikTok is much more durational. To keep someone on a platform of that type for as long as possible, it’s going to wind up favoring different kinds of things.
paras.zh: [政治内容][在这些平台上]并不像在 Facebook 上那样具有独特的优势，[因为]短视频平台上广告销售的盈利方式存在差异。它们更有可能按观看次数出售。 TikTok 的算法持续时间更长。为了让某人尽可能长时间地留在这种类型的平台上，最终会偏向于不同类型的事物。

paras.en: It’s creating different kinds of problems; [for example], the eating disorder problem continues to be very real. There remains a big conspiracy theory problem, particularly around things that get monetized. But the political extremism problem is not as severe—not because anybody really did anything [to address] it but because this other form of social media that just was able to capture people’s attention longer and better became more dominant, and it’s prone to different problems.
paras.zh: 它造成了不同类型的问题； [例如]，饮食失调问题仍然是非常现实的。仍然存在一个很大的阴谋论问题，尤其是在货币化的事物方面。但政治极端主义问题并没有那么严重，不是因为有人真正采取了任何措施来解决这个问题，而是因为这种另一种形式的社交媒体能够更长时间、更好地吸引人们的注意力，变得更加占主导地位，而且很容易出现不同的问题。

paras.en: What are your final thoughts on the film?
paras.zh: 您对这部电影的最终想法是什么？

paras.en: It got a lot of small things that I knew about right. The movie made it very legible why Jeff did what he did and why Frances did what she did. But I did not find that movie very enlightening as to why Mark Zuckerberg does what he does.
paras.zh: 它有很多我所知道的小事情。这部电影非常清楚地说明了为什么杰夫做了他所做的事情以及为什么弗朗西斯做了她所做的事情。但我并没有发现这部电影对于马克·扎克伯格为什么要做他所做的事情很有启发性。

paras.en: I think we all like to think, when there are such obvious bad things happening in the world, that it’s because there’s a villain twirling their mustache and making the bad thing happen.
paras.zh: 我想我们都喜欢认为，当世界上发生如此明显的坏事时，那是因为有一个坏人捻着胡子，让坏事发生。

paras.en: But I think a lot of bad things in the world happen because good people let them. Or good people have other reasons for finding that bad thing to be tolerable. I think it would be more useful to understand that as a way of getting to “How can we make social media safer for people?”
paras.zh: 但我认为世界上很多坏事的发生都是因为好人让它们发生的。或者好人有其他理由认为坏事是可以容忍的。我认为理解这一点作为了解“我们如何让社交媒体对人们来说更安全？”的一种方式会更有用。

articles.title: Your voice is more than sound. It’s part of who you are
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: Meet Jules Rodriguez. He’s a dad, husband, former science teacher, podcaster and stand-up comedian — someone who has always had a lot to say.
paras.zh: 认识朱尔斯·罗德里格斯。他是一位父亲、丈夫、前科学老师、播客和单口喜剧演员——一个总是有很多话要说的人。

paras.en: But ALS has taken away his ability to speak. Now, Jules communicates by typing with his eyes, and an AI-generated voice clone speaks his words aloud.
paras.zh: 但肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）已经剥夺了他说话的能力。现在，朱尔斯通过眼睛打字进行交流，人工智能生成的语音克隆会大声说出他的话。

paras.en: In this episode of The Deep End, hear Jules’ story, as well as perspectives from scientists and clinicians on why a voice is so much more than a way to communicate. Human brains are poised to seek out voices, and all the various kinds of information they can hold.
paras.zh: 在这一集中的《The Deep End》中，聆听朱尔斯的故事，以及科学家和临床医生对为什么声音不仅仅是一种交流方式的看法。人类的大脑随时准备寻找声音以及它们所能容纳的各种信息。

paras.en: Jules’ experience reveals just how much of our identity is created by the way we sound — and what it means when that sound disappears.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯的经历揭示了我们的身份在多大程度上是由我们发声的方式决定的——以及当声音消失时意味着什么。

paras.en: Laura Sanders: Jules Rodriguez has always had a lot to say. He has talked to kids as their science teacher. He’s talked about his life for years on a podcast he created with his wife.
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：朱尔斯·罗德里格斯总是有很多话要说。他作为孩子们的科学老师与他们交谈。多年来，他一直在与妻子共同创建的播客中谈论自己的生活。

paras.en: Jules: Hey everyone, it’s been a while and I am so excited to be back.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：大家好，已经有一段时间了，我很高兴能回来。

paras.en: Sanders: He even does some of the most terrifying talking I can imagine. He performs in front of crowds as a stand-up comedian.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他甚至说了一些我能想象到的最可怕的言论。他作为一名单口喜剧演员在人群面前表演。

paras.en: Jules: I have to pick my battles. Do I want to be right or do I want to eat tonight?
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我必须选择我的战斗。我想要是对的还是我今晚想吃东西？

paras.en: Sanders: His wife, Maria Aleandra Fernandez, who goes by MA, says that Jules’ voice is one of her very favorites.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他的妻子玛丽亚·阿利安德拉·费尔南德斯（Maria Aleandra Fernandez）（简称 MA）说朱尔斯的声音是她最喜欢的声音之一。

paras.en: MA: Oh man, I definitely love hearing Jules’ voice. I’m not just saying that, but I do.
paras.zh: MA：天啊，我真的很喜欢听朱尔斯的声音。我不仅这么说，而且确实这么做了。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules was born and raised in Miami. He and MA have a nine-year-old son named Skyler. Jules loves baseball. He loves the Marlins. He loves being outside. He loves action.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯在迈阿密出生和长大。他和马云有一个九岁的儿子，名叫斯凯勒。朱尔斯喜欢棒球。他喜欢马林鱼队。他喜欢呆在外面。他热爱行动。

paras.en: Jules: I was always pretty high energy. I loved mountain biking, snorkeling, fishing, and playing all sports, really. Baseball is my favorite sport to play and watch.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我总是精力充沛。我真的很喜欢山地自行车、浮潜、钓鱼以及所有运动。棒球是我最喜欢玩和观看的运动。

paras.en: Sanders: The night Jules and MA met, they were doing karaoke at her 30th birthday party.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯和妈妈见面的那天晚上，他们正在她 30 岁生日聚会上唱卡拉 OK。

paras.en: MA: A friend introduced us, and it was kind of a, sort of a love at first sight situation. We danced, we sang.
paras.zh: MA：一位朋友介绍我们认识的，这是一种一见钟情的情况。我们跳舞，我们唱歌。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules’ karaoke song choice was a classic that no millennial can resist. It was Sir Mix-A-Lot’s “Baby Got Back.”
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯选择的卡拉 OK 歌曲是千禧一代无法抗拒的经典之作。这是 Mix-A-Lot 爵士的《宝贝回来了》。

paras.en: MA: “Baby Got Back,” yeah. That one he got up there and sang with a couple of his friends. It was like him and his three other buddies that were there with him. And oh, that was just so joyous. And we had karaoke at our wedding as well, so, we’ve always loved to sing, to dance. We took ballroom dancing classes. We, like, danced at every wedding. All of it. So, yeah.
paras.zh: MA：“宝贝回来了”，是的。那首歌他站起来和他的几个朋友一起唱。就像他和他的另外三个伙伴一样。哦，那真是太令人高兴了。我们的婚礼上也有卡拉OK，所以，我们一直喜欢唱歌、跳舞。我们参加了交谊舞课程。我们就像在每次婚礼上跳舞一样。所有这一切。所以，是的。

paras.en: Sanders: One more thing about Jules. He has ALS. That’s short for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, a disease also known as Lou Gehrig’s disease or motor neuron disease. Jules has lived with ALS since 2020. Many of his muscles no longer respond to his brain’s signals, which means he can’t move his body or breathe on his own. This dropped signal between brain and body also means that Jules is no longer able to talk. That line you heard earlier from Jules?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：关于朱尔斯的另一件事。他患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症。这是肌萎缩侧索硬化症的缩写，这种疾病也称为卢伽雷氏病或运动神经元病。 Jules 自 2020 年以来一直患有 ALS。他的许多肌肉不再对大脑的信号做出反应，这意味着他无法移动身体或自行呼吸。大脑和身体之间的信号丢失也意味着朱尔斯不再能够说话。你之前从朱尔斯那里听到过这句话吗？

paras.en: Sanders: That was an AI-generated, synthetic voice speaking his words. His voice, as it used to exist, is gone.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是人工智能生成的合成声音，说出了他的话。他的声音，就像以前那样，已经消失了。

paras.en: Welcome to Season 2 of The Deep End, a podcast about our brains and ourselves. I’m your host, Laura Sanders, a reporter with Science News. And this season, called Talk to Me, is about the human voice.
paras.zh: 欢迎来到 The Deep End 第二季，这是一个关于我们的大脑和我们自己的播客。我是主持人劳拉·桑德斯 (Laura Sanders)，是《科学新闻》的记者。这一季名为《跟我说话》，讲述的是人类的声音。

paras.en: [intro] Hey Mom, can I tell you something? The casual observer sees little of the vigorous activity at the site of voice production. The voice is absolutely an integral part of your identity. Do you want to talk? That added layer of it being you. Hello? Your voice. Hi. Your voice is you.
paras.zh: [简介] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？不经意的观察者几乎看不到声音产生处的剧烈活动。声音绝对是您身份的一个组成部分。你想说话吗？那增加的一层就是你。你好？你的声音。你好。你的声音就是你。

paras.en: [voice] My poor little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of their skin but by the content of their character. I have a dream…
paras.zh: [声音]我可怜的孩子们有一天会生活在一个国家，在那里他们将不会根据他们的肤色而是根据他们的性格内容来评判。我有一个梦想…

paras.en: Sanders: Voices can be powerful. We save and replay voicemails.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音是有力量的。我们保存并重播语音邮件。

paras.en: [voice] Hey, dude, I’m just calling to say hi and chit-chat.
paras.zh: [声音]嘿，伙计，我打电话只是想打个招呼，聊聊。

paras.en: Sanders: We call someone special just to hear their voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我们打电话给特别的人只是为了听听他们的声音。

paras.en: Sanders: We love to hear people tell stories.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我们喜欢听人们讲故事。

paras.en: Sanders: But why? What is it inside these voices that can calm us down or terrify us or have us laughing so hard we’re gasping for air? In this season, we’re going to explore a simple but deep question. What gives the human voice so much power? You’re going to hear all sorts of voices. They’ll tell a story of what connects us and what happens when those connections are lost. Over the next six episodes, we’ll explore a new digital world. In this world, human voices no longer need a human body to create them. You’ll hear how machines can speak for those who can’t, and even pull words from the brains of people who can’t speak. It’s a story about how technology is changing the human voice in ways that are good, bad, and fascinating. Let’s begin.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是为什么呢？这些声音里到底有什么东西可以让我们平静下来，或者让我们感到恐惧，或者让我们笑得喘不过气来？在这一季中，我们将探讨一个简单而深刻的问题。是什么赋予人类声音如此强大的力量？你会听到各种各样的声音。他们将讲述一个故事，讲述是什么将我们联系在一起，以及当这些联系消失时会发生什么。在接下来的六集中，我们将探索一个新的数字世界。在这个世界上，人类的声音不再需要人体来创造。你会听到机器如何为那些不会说话的人说话，甚至从不会说话的人的大脑中提取单词。这是一个关于技术如何以好的、坏的和令人着迷的方式改变人类声音的故事。让我们开始吧。

paras.en: Sanders: People listen for voices in everything. There’s a parallel you might have heard of. It’s a weird quirk of human brains that we’re able to find faces everywhere, too. That’s why you’ve seen the shape of a face in an electrical outlet or a car grill or a random pattern on the wall. Our brains love seeing faces. And it turns out our brains love hearing voices too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：人们在一切事情上都会倾听声音。您可能听说过一个类似的情况。我们也能够在任何地方找到面孔，这也是人类大脑的一个奇怪的怪癖。这就是为什么你会在电源插座或汽车烤架上看到一张脸的形状，或者在墙上看到随机的图案。我们的大脑喜欢看到面孔。事实证明我们的大脑也喜欢听声音。

paras.en: Greg Bryant: It’s really well established that there’s a voice-selective region and it’s activated really early.
paras.zh: 格雷格·布莱恩特：确实存在一个声音选择区域，而且它很早就被激活了。

paras.en: Sanders: Greg Bryant is a cognitive scientist who studies vocal communications at UCLA. He tells me that there’s a spot in the brain that responds strongly to voices.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：格雷格·布莱恩特是一位认知科学家，在加州大学洛杉矶分校研究声音交流。他告诉我，大脑中有一个地方对声音反应强烈。

paras.en: Bryant: Yeah, we hear voices in all kinds of stuff. I mean, you ever been out camping and you’re like [whispers], you know, or something, you know, you hear like whispering. And yeah, it’s really easy to hallucinate a voice.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：是的，我们听到各种各样的声音。我的意思是，你曾经出去露营，你就像[窃窃私语]，你知道，或者什么，你知道，你听到像窃窃私语。是的，我们很容易产生幻觉。

paras.en: Sanders: Part of the reason our brains tune into voices might be that they are packed with information, information that goes well beyond words.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我们的大脑适应声音的部分原因可能是它们充满了信息，这些信息远远超出了语言的范围。

paras.en: Bryant: It’s definitely a very intimate entryway to a person because you get emotion, history, your body, all in one quick auditory signal. So I think it’s very personal. It gives you access to a person’s individual nature. And it contains language and vocal emotions in a way that’s very direct and evocative. It’s one of the most personal things that you encounter with another person.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：这绝对是一个人的非常亲密的入口，因为你可以通过一个快速的听觉信号获得情感、历史、你的身体。所以我认为这是非常个人化的。它使您可以了解一个人的个性。它以一种非常直接和令人回味的方式包含语言和声音情感。这是你与另一个人遇到的最私人的事情之一。

paras.en: Sanders: Voices are also some of the first social inputs a baby gets.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音也是婴儿获得的第一个社交输入之一。

paras.en: Sanders: In utero, a baby hears a mother’s voice all day, singing to the radio, ordering a smoothie, talking to coworkers. This voice, carried on waves through the amniotic fluid, makes a big impression.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在子宫里，婴儿整天都会听到母亲的声音，对着收音机唱歌，点一杯冰沙，与同事交谈。这种声音通过羊水通过波传播，给人留下了深刻的印象。

paras.en: Bryant: Kids hear voices actually before they’re even born. That’s one of the most salient auditory stimuli in utero, right? That they know their mother’s voice before they’re even born, and even have picked up aspects of the rhythm and the language they speak before they’re born. So it’s just something the brain is just attracted to right from the beginning of development. Because I think it’s such an important source of information about the people around you and what’s happening.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：孩子们在出生之前就已经听到了声音。这是子宫内最显着的听觉刺激之一，对吗？他们甚至在出生之前就知道母亲的声音，甚至在出生之前就已经掌握了母亲所说的节奏和语言的某些方面。所以这只是大脑从发育之初就被吸引的东西。因为我认为这是关于你周围的人和正在发生的事情的重要信息来源。

paras.en: Sanders: People’s voices are both extremely common and at the same time special and unique. So when people are faced with the prospect of losing their voice, which is what happens to most people with ALS, including Jules, they’re looking at a profound loss.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：人们的声音既极其普遍，同时又特殊且独特。因此，当人们面临失去声音的前景时，这就是大多数肌萎缩侧索硬化症患者（包括朱尔斯）都会发生的情况，他们面临着巨大的损失。

paras.en: Kate Nilson: So much. So much is in a voice.
paras.zh: 凯特·尼尔森：就这么多。声音里蕴藏着如此多的内容。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s speech-language pathologist Kate Nilson. She works with people who anticipate that they will lose the ability to talk, including people with ALS. She uses lots of tools to help people plan for this eventuality. That includes recording messages for use later on and banking their voice, a method that allows typed words to be spoken by a computer program. In recent years, her job has expanded as she works with people to create fancy AI-powered voice clones.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是言语病理学家凯特·尼尔森。她与那些预计自己将失去说话能力的人一起工作，其中包括肌萎缩侧索硬化症患者。她使用许多工具来帮助人们为这种可能性做好计划。这包括录制消息以供以后使用以及存储他们的声音，这是一种允许计算机程序说出键入的单词的方法。近年来，她的工作范围不断扩大，她与人们合作创建由人工智能驱动的精美语音克隆。

paras.en: Nilson: When I am a clinician in the clinic and someone has just gotten the diagnosis, they’re oftentimes told that there’s not a lot they can do, right? There’s not a lot of treatments out there. We’re working on it, but there’s not a lot of treatments currently. There’s no exercises to make you stronger. This is something they can do. So a lot of times, I can do this. This is something that I can do to be proactive and to be ready for the future. So there’s that.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：当我是诊所的临床医生并且有人刚刚得到诊断时，他们经常被告知他们无能为力，对吧？那里没有太多的治疗方法。我们正在研究这个问题，但目前还没有很多治疗方法。没有任何练习可以让你变得更强壮。这是他们可以做的事情。所以很多时候，我都能做到这一点。这是我可以采取的积极主动并为未来做好准备的事情。就是这样。

paras.en: Sanders: Nilson’s perspective means that she sees up close and personal the meaning and the importance of a person’s voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：尼尔森的视角意味着她能够近距离地、个人地看到一个人声音的意义和重要性。

paras.en: Nilson: There’s also thinking that these messages, these voices, can be saved by the family forever. And so that means a lot to people. But most importantly, what is really hard until you’re in it is how much your voice is you.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：还有人认为这些信息、这些声音可以被家人永远保存。所以这对人们来说意义重大。但最重要的是，在你真正融入其中之前，真正困难的是你的声音在多大程度上是你自己。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules uses an assistive device that lets him type by looking at letters and words on a screen. His synthetic voice then reads what he has just typed with his eyes. For this story, I also interviewed a man named Patrick Darling, who communicates with typed words and a voice clone that speaks them. Patrick is 33 and lives in Bristol, England.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯使用一种辅助设备，让他通过查看屏幕上的字母和单词来打字。然后他的合成声音会用眼睛读出他刚刚输入的内容。在这个故事中，我还采访了一位名叫帕特里克·达林（Patrick Darling）的人，他通过打字和说话的语音克隆进行交流。帕特里克 (Patrick) 33 岁，住在英国布里斯托尔。

paras.en: Patrick Darling: I’ve been a barista, a barber, boatman, a gamer, a painter, a voice actor, Youtube content creator and a musician.
paras.zh: Patrick Darling：我做过咖啡师、理发师、船夫、游戏玩家、画家、配音演员、Youtube 内容创作者和音乐家。

paras.en: Sanders: Patrick was diagnosed with ALS in 2022. Since then, the disease has taken a lot from him, including his voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：帕特里克于 2022 年被诊断出患有 ALS。从那时起，这种疾病就夺走了他的很多东西，包括他的声音。

paras.en: Patrick: Now four years later, I have lost the ability to sing and play my instruments.
paras.zh: 帕特里克：四年过去了，我已经失去了唱歌和演奏乐器的能力。

paras.en: Patrick: Being unable to talk is extremely isolating, unbelievably frustrating and oftentimes frightening. I think people who don’t really know you often feel uncomfortable by your silence and I think it’s easy for people to forget that there is still a person stuck in there.
paras.zh: 帕特里克：无法说话是一种极度孤立、令人难以置信的沮丧，而且常常令人恐惧。我认为那些不太了解你的人常常会对你的沉默感到不舒服，而且我认为人们很容易忘记还有一个人被困在那里。

paras.en: Sanders: Patrick’s description of feeling forgotten, of the isolation and fear that comes from not being able to talk, came up again and again as I reported this story. To step back here, the loss of a voice is one loss of many. ALS progresses differently for everyone, but its hallmark is a loss of movement. The disease interrupts the signals from the brain to the muscles, meaning that people lose the ability to button a shirt or apply their mascara or walk. How scary, how frustrating, how deeply annoying it must be to not be able to move in the ways you need. As I’m talking to Jules and MA on a video call, there are a few times this hits home. For instance, when a gnat starts circling Jules.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：帕特里克描述的被遗忘的感觉、无法说话所带来的孤立和恐惧，在我报道这个故事时一次又一次地出现。退一步讲，失去声音是许多人的损失之一。每个人的 ALS 进展情况都不同，但其特点是运动能力丧失。这种疾病会中断从大脑到肌肉的信号，这意味着人们无法扣衬衫、涂睫毛膏或走路。无法按照你需要的方式行动，这是多么可怕、多么令人沮丧、多么令人烦恼。当我在视频通话中与朱尔斯和马云交谈时，有几次这句话击中了我的要害。例如，当一只蚊子开始围着朱尔斯转时。

paras.en: MA: He has a little fly flying around. Can you imagine not being able to swat away a gnat? Yeah. Torture chamber. Yeah.
paras.zh: MA：他有一只小苍蝇在飞来飞去。你能想象无法赶走一只蚊子吗？是的。酷刑室。是的。

paras.en: Sanders: On top of not being able to swat the gnat, if Jules didn’t have a way to communicate, he couldn’t even ask MA to swat the gnat for him. He couldn’t say he’s annoyed or thirsty or that he’s getting pinched by something. He couldn’t ask her to turn off whatever machine is beeping and driving him crazy. It’s hard to imagine. In a class Kate Nilson teaches at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, she asks her students, who are all future speech pathologists, to experience a tiny sliver of what it must feel like to not talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：除了无法拍掉蚊子之外，如果朱尔斯没有办法沟通，他甚至无法要求妈妈帮他拍掉蚊子。他不能说自己生气、口渴，或者被什么东西夹住了。他不能要求她关掉任何发出嘟嘟声、让他发疯的机器。很难想象。凯特·尼尔森 (Kate Nilson) 在明尼苏达大学双城分校 (University of Minnesota Twin Cities) 教授的一堂课上，她要求她的学生（他们都是未来的语言病理学家）体验一下不说话的感觉。

paras.en: Nilson: One of the assignments that I assign to my class is that they have to put an app on their phone and they can’t talk for two hours. They have to go for two hours not talking, but only using an app on their phone just to get that experience of what that is like.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：我给班级布置的作业之一是，他们必须在手机上安装一个应用程序，并且两个小时内不能说话。他们必须花两个小时不说话，只使用手机上的应用程序，才能体验到那种感觉。

paras.en: Sanders: When they wanted to say something, Nielsen’s students used their phones to type the words, and then a robotic voice read them aloud. They told her that during the exercise, they stopped trying to say what they were thinking as much, and how lonely that felt.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当他们想说些什么时，尼尔森的学生用手机输入单词，然后机器人声音大声朗读它们。他们告诉她，在练习过程中，他们不再试图说出自己的想法，以及那种感觉是多么孤独。

paras.en: Nilson: And here these are, you know, 24-year-old speech pathology grad students, and so many of them in their reflection back to me say, “I didn’t realize how much my voice is who I am.”
paras.zh: 尼尔森：你知道，这些都是 24 岁的言语病理学研究生，他们中的许多人在向我反映时说，“我没有意识到我的声音在多大程度上代表了我自己。”

paras.en: Sanders: They had things to say, but they didn’t, because of the time and the effort it would take.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他们有话要说，但他们没有说，因为这需要时间和精力。

paras.en: Nilson: If anyone listening is curious, I would just encourage you to try that. And then you see what that is like and what it feels like to have so much to say and not be able to say it, and what that takes away from your personality and who you are. And not even not being able to say it, but not being able to say it in your voice. It’s so much who we are that it’s, it’s hard to explain. It’s more of a feeling. But it’s a big one.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：如果有人好奇，我会鼓励你尝试一下。然后你就会明白那是什么感觉，有那么多话要说却又无法说出来是什么感觉，以及这会剥夺你的个性和你是谁。甚至不是不能说出来，而是不能用你的声音说出来。我们是谁，很难解释。这更多的是一种感觉。但这是一件大事。

paras.en: Sanders: I did her assignment too. I’ll come clean here and say that I procrastinated a lot. There was never a good day for me to not talk. I had to lead a meeting. I was coaching soccer. And that, in and of itself, is informative because it tells me just how important my voice is to me. So I finally got around to it. It was hard. I used a straightforward, no bells and whistles app on my phone. I typed words and then a pleasant but quite robotic woman’s voice named Samantha in the app spoke them aloud for me as I went through my day.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我也完成了她的任务。我会在这里坦白说我拖延了很多。对我来说，没有一天是不说话的好日子。我必须主持一次会议。我当时正在教足球。这本身就具有丰富的信息，因为它告诉我我的声音对我来说有多重要。所以我终于抽出时间来做这件事。这很难。我在手机上使用了一个简单、没有花里胡哨的应用程序。我输入文字，然后应用程序中一个名叫萨曼莎（Samantha）的愉快但相当机器人的女人的声音在我度过这一天时为我大声朗读它们。

paras.en: [voice] Would you like cereal for breakfast? What kind? Cheerios? Honey Nut Crunch?
paras.zh: [声音] 早餐想吃麦片吗？什么样的？麦片？蜂蜜坚果脆饼？

paras.en: Sanders: The logistical stuff was tricky, especially for a rushed morning.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：后勤工作很棘手，尤其是在一个匆忙的早晨。

paras.en: [voice]: Did you brush your teeth? Daddy will drive you to school. He is leaving in five minutes.
paras.zh: [声音]：你刷牙了吗？爸爸会开车送你去学校。他五分钟后就要离开。

paras.en: Sanders: I couldn’t call the cats inside. Listen.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我无法叫里面的猫。听。

paras.en: [voice] Here, kitty, kitty, kitty. Come on. Bonnie, Arlo, here, kitty, kitty, kitty.
paras.zh: [声音] 在这里，小猫，小猫，小猫。快点。邦妮，阿洛，在这里，小猫，小猫，小猫。

paras.en: Sanders: But what was harder, I realized later, were the moments I couldn’t or didn’t connect.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但后来我意识到，更困难的是我无法或无法联系的时刻。

paras.en: Sanders: It was hard to ask my kids if they had any dreams the night before.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：很难问我的孩子们前一天晚上是否做了梦。

paras.en: Sanders: I couldn’t say a quick hello to a friend at the gym. Instead, I smiled extra big at her and felt pretty awkward about it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我无法在健身房与朋友快速打招呼。相反，我对她笑得很开心，并感到很尴尬。

paras.en: Sanders: I understood a bit more about what Patrick meant about feeling isolated. I stopped trying to connect. I self-censored. I didn’t have to stop. After all, I had the technology to communicate in my literal hand, but it felt too hard, too slow, too artificial. It didn’t feel like it was worth the effort for me to type and to ask other people to slow down and listen. My brief experiment gave me a glimpse, a tiny glimpse, into a life without a voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我对帕特里克感到孤立的含义有了更多的了解。我停止尝试连接。我自我审查。我不必停下来。毕竟，我拥有可以用我的双手进行交流的技术，但感觉太难、太慢、太人工。我觉得不值得我费力打字并要求其他人放慢速度倾听。我短暂的实验让我瞥见了一个没有声音的生活。

paras.en: Piotrowski: Being able to ask for things, being able to tell someone when you are in pain. Or when you’re feeling good, or when something that they do is helpful.
paras.zh: Piotrowski：能够提出要求，能够在痛苦时告诉别人。或者当你感觉良好时，或者当他们做的事情有帮助时。

paras.en: Sanders: Speech-language pathologist Jessica Piotrowski works at the UC Davis Center for Voice and Swallowing. She helps people who are losing their ability to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：言语病理学家杰西卡·皮奥特罗斯基在加州大学戴维斯分校声音和吞咽中心工作。她帮助那些失去说话能力的人。

paras.en: Pietrowski: The interesting thing that I have learned in working in this field, and I’m not sure if the general public is aware, is that for many of these individuals, losing their speech is way more devastating than losing their mobility. You know, you think you think about what these individuals often are unfortunately losing: their mobility, their independence, their swallowing. But being able to communicate is going to, in some way, help them a little bit through all those things. And going through all of those changes without a voice or a way to kind of be yourself just makes them so much harder and just to be able to express yourself and to maintain a little more of a sense of dignity of like, this is who I am. This disease is not going to take that. I still have my voice. I still have my sense of humor. I still have my emotion that I can hopefully in the coming future express to people. It’s just so, so important.
paras.zh: 彼得罗夫斯基：我在这一领域的工作中学到的一件有趣的事情是，对于其中许多人来说，失去言语比失去行动能力更具破坏性，我不确定公众是否意识到这一点。你知道，你想想这些人经常不幸失去的东西：他们的行动能力、他们的独立性、他们的吞咽能力。但能够沟通将在某种程度上帮助他们解决所有这些问题。在没有声音或没有办法做自己的情况下经历所有这些变化只会让它们变得更加困难，而只是能够表达自己并保持更多的尊严感，这就是我。这种疾病不会接受这个。我仍然有我的声音。我仍然有我的幽默感。我仍然有我的情感，希望在不久的将来能够向人们表达。这就是如此、如此重要。

paras.en: Sanders: In 2022, two years after his ALS diagnosis, Jules’ voice started slipping away. MA had already thought about this inevitable moment, and she was dreading it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2022 年，即朱尔斯诊断出 ALS 两年后，朱尔斯的声音开始消失。妈妈已经想到了这个不可避免的时刻，她很害怕它。

paras.en: MA: Thinking back when I was at that time, and he was losing all of his physical abilities, you know, little by little, it’s like, you can no longer do this, and then that, and then that, and then that. And I always remember thinking, all of these things are breaking my heart, but when he loses his voice, I’m just going to shatter into a million pieces.
paras.zh: 马：回想我当时的情况，他的身体能力都在丧失，你知道，一点一点地，你不能再做这个，然后那个，然后那个，然后那个。我总是记得我在想，所有这些事情都让我心碎，但当他失去声音时，我就会碎成一百万块。

paras.en: Sanders: On the next episode of Talk To Me.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在《跟我说话》的下一集里。

paras.en: MA: I still remember the first time, this was in 2022, the summer of 22, that I heard the first little crack in his voice that let me know something’s changing.
paras.zh: MA：我还记得第一次，那是在 2022 年，也就是 22 号的夏天，我听到他声音中的第一个小裂痕，让我知道有些事情正在发生变化。

paras.en: Sanders: What does it feel like to stare down a future without a voice, especially for Jules? On his long-running podcast with MA, they talk about their lives, their family, their life that they’re building. They also talk about his ALS.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在没有声音的情况下展望未来是什么感觉，尤其是对朱尔斯来说？在他与 MA 的长期播客中，他们谈论他们的生活、他们的家庭、他们正在建设的生活。他们还谈论了他的 ALS。

paras.en: Jules: It’s strange with the podcast because you can hear my real voice slowly decay till we stop.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：播客很奇怪，因为你可以听到我真实的声音慢慢衰减，直到我们停止。

paras.en: MA: Yeah, it really is this archive of what he sounded like little by little as it changed. And it was, yeah, like very disarming to get to that moment. And then you begin to get used to it, and you sort of work around it and you appreciate that it’s still there. But that was, yeah, that was really, really difficult for me.
paras.zh: MA：是的，这确实是他听起来一点一点改变的档案。是的，那一刻让人非常放松。然后你开始习惯它，你可以解决它，你会感激它仍然存在。但这对我来说真的非常困难。

paras.en: Sanders: How much of Jules was his voice?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他的声音有多少是朱尔斯的？

paras.en: Jules: For me, it felt like I was fading away. Like when Marty McFly was seeing his family fade away in the picture he had in “Back to the Future.”
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：对我来说，感觉就像我正在消失。就像马蒂·麦克弗莱在《回到未来》的照片中看到他的家人逐渐消失一样。

paras.en: Sanders: This is The Deep End, Season 2, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you liked this podcast, tell your friends. If you really like this podcast, leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts at sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：《这里是深渊》第二季，《跟我说话》。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友。如果您真的喜欢这个播客，请给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。通过 sciencenews.org 的播客向我们发送您的问题和评论。

paras.en: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor-in-chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特 (Nancy Shute) 是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: Here’s a look at the Nobel Prizes for science
articles.author: Nikk Ogasa

paras.en: It’s Nobels season — that time of the year when we find out which groundbreaking, paradigm-shifting, world-changing achievements beat out the rest to win what is arguably the most prestigious award on Earth.
paras.zh: 现在是诺贝尔奖季——一年中的这个时候，我们会找出哪些突破性、范式转变、改变世界的成就击败其他成就，赢得可以说是地球上最负盛名的奖项。

paras.en: From a light switch for the brain to the discovery of an ultra-elusive subatomic particle hailing from beyond our solar system to a solution to one of the most enduring puzzles in all of organic chemistry, the researchers behind this year’s scientific prizes each revolutionized the ways that scientists understand the world around them.
paras.zh: 从大脑的光开关到发现来自太阳系之外的极其难以捉摸的亚原子粒子，再到解决有机化学中最持久的难题之一，今年科学奖项背后的研究人员都彻底改变了科学家理解周围世界的方式。

paras.en: Take a look at the science behind each of this year’s awards.
paras.zh: 看看今年每个奖项背后的科学原理。

paras.en: A galaxy of nearly 90 billion neurons exists within a single human brain. But unlike stars in the void, neurons communicate with one another via some 100 trillion connections, allowing the human mind to learn, adapt and interact with its surroundings.
paras.zh: 一个人脑内存在一个由近 900 亿个神经元组成的星系。但与虚空中的星星不同的是，神经元通过约 100 万亿个连接相互通信，使人类思维能够学习、适应周围环境并与之互动。

paras.en: For scientists to understand how individual actions arise from such complexity, they needed a tool to directly link neural circuits to specific behaviors, said Abdel El Manira, a neuroscientist at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm. “Neuroscientists dreamed of a neuronal switch, a tool to turn specific neurons on or off with great precision,” El Manira said during the Oct. 5 announcement of this year’s prize in physiology or medicine by the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institute.
paras.zh: 斯德哥尔摩卡罗林斯卡研究所的神经科学家阿卜杜勒·埃尔·马尼拉 (Abdel El Manira) 表示，为了让科学家了解个体行为如何从如此复杂的情况中产生，他们需要一种工具将神经回路与特定行为直接联系起来。 “神经科学家梦想有一个神经元开关，一种能够非常精确地打开或关闭特定神经元的工具，”埃尔·马尼拉在卡罗林斯卡学院诺贝尔大会 10 月 5 日宣布今年的生理学或医学奖时说道。

paras.en: Enter the bright idea that won. It’s a technology called optogenetics, which involves using light to precisely activate specific cells, like neurons, and watch how behavior changes. For their foundational contributions to optogenetics, biophysicists Peter Hegemann of Humboldt University in Berlin and Georg Nagel, of the Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg in Germany, and neuroscientist Karl Deisseroth of Stanford University shared this year’s prize.
paras.zh: 输入获胜的好主意。这是一种称为光遗传学的技术，涉及利用光精确激活特定细胞（例如神经元），并观察行为如何变化。柏林洪堡大学的生物物理学家 Peter Hegemann 和德国维尔茨堡朱利叶斯·马克西米利安大学的 Georg Nagel 以及斯坦福大学的神经科学家 Karl Deisseroth 分享了今年的奖项，以表彰他们对光遗传学的基础性贡献。

paras.en: The prize winners’ story starts in an unlikely place: the eye spot of a single celled green alga called Chlamydomonas. In the early 2000s, Hegemann, then at the Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry in Martinsreid, Germany, and Nagel, at the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics in Frankfurt, discovered a unique protein in the alga’s eye spot. When illuminated, the protein generated an electrical impulse, enabling the organism to move. Further research revealed that when the protein, called channelrhodopsin, was exposed to light, it opened like a pore, allowing positively charged ions to flow into a cell, generating the electrical impulse. “They had just discovered the switch neuroscientists had long dreamed of,” El Manira said.
paras.zh: 获奖者的故事始于一个意想不到的地方：一种称为衣藻的单细胞绿藻的眼点。 2000 年代初，当时在德国马丁斯里德马克斯普朗克生物化学研究所工作的赫格曼和在法兰克福马克斯普朗克生物物理研究所工作的内格尔在藻类的眼斑中发现了一种独特的蛋白质。当光照时，蛋白质产生电脉冲，使生物体能够移动。进一步的研究表明，当这种称为通道视紫红质的蛋白质暴露在光下时，它会像孔一样打开，允许带正电的离子流入细胞，产生电脉冲。 “他们刚刚发现了神经科学家梦寐以求的转变，”埃尔马尼拉说。

paras.en: Building on the Hegemann and Nagel’s work, Deisseroth began testing whether channelrhodopsin could be used to activate brain cells. He and his colleagues first inserted the gene for channelrhodopsin into cultures of rat nerve cells and found that the cells reacted to light instantaneously. They then introduced the gene into nerve cells in the brains of living mice, along with optical fibers fed through the rodents’ skulls. By beaming blue light through the fibers, the researchers were able to control the movements of the rodents’ whiskers. This technology gave researchers the ability to test the links between certain brain circuits and behaviors.
paras.zh: 在 Hegemann 和 Nagel 的工作基础上，Deisseroth 开始测试视紫红质通道蛋白是否可用于激活脑细胞。他和他的同事首先将视紫红质通道蛋白基因插入大鼠神经细胞培养物中，发现细胞对光立即做出反应。然后，他们将该基因引入活体小鼠大脑的神经细胞中，同时将光纤引入啮齿类动物的头骨中。通过通过纤维发射蓝光，研究人员能够控制啮齿动物胡须的运动。这项技术使研究人员能够测试某些大脑回路和行为之间的联系。

paras.en: “The technology, which soon became known as optogenetics, transformed neuroscience,” El Manira said. In addition to exposing the inner workings of healthy brains, he noted, “it has also helped reveal how brain circuits are disrupted, with implications for conditions such as blindness, depression and dementia.”
paras.zh: “这项技术很快被称为光遗传学，它改变了神经科学，”埃尔马尼拉说。他指出，除了揭示健康大脑的内部运作之外，“它还有助于揭示大脑回路如何被破坏，从而对失明、抑郁和痴呆等疾病产生影响。”

paras.en: For example, the technology has been used improve vision in some patients with retinitis pigmentosa, a disease that degrades light-sensing cells in the retina. It’s also helping researchers investigate the role that a person’s heart plays in how they experience and interact with their surroundings.
paras.zh: 例如，该技术已被用于改善一些患有色素性视网膜炎的患者的视力，这种疾病会降低视网膜中的光敏细胞的功能。它还帮助研究人员调查一个人的心脏在他们如何体验和与周围环境互动中所扮演的角色。

paras.en: At the South Pole, there exists a block of ice unlike any other on Earth. Buried deep beneath the surface of the Antarctic ice sheet, a cubic kilometer of ice is threaded with thousands of beadlike sensors. Known as the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, this immense instrument enables researchers to detect the most elusive particle in the universe — the neutrino.
paras.zh: 在南极，有一块与地球上其他地方不同的冰块。深埋在南极冰盖表面下方，一立方公里的冰上布满了数千个珠状传感器。这个巨大的仪器被称为冰立方中微子观测站，使研究人员能够探测宇宙中最难以捉摸的粒子——中微子。

paras.en: Detecting neutrinos from beyond our solar system had been a goal of scientists for decades, as that could help understand where and how the universe accelerates particles to extraordinary energies.
paras.zh: 几十年来，探测太阳系以外的中微子一直是科学家的目标，因为这可以帮助了解宇宙在何处以及如何将粒子加速到非凡的能量。

paras.en: The researcher who led the creation of the Antarctic observatory, physicist Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin–Madison, received this year’s Nobel Prize in physics. Halzen was awarded “for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin,” Mark Pearce, a physicist and chair of the Nobel committee for physics, during the Oct. 6 announcement by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: 领导创建南极天文台的研究人员、威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的物理学家弗朗西斯·哈尔岑获得了今年的诺贝尔物理学奖。瑞典皇家科学院在 10 月 6 日宣布，诺贝尔物理学委员会主席、物理学家马克·皮尔斯 (Mark Pearce) 授予哈尔岑奖，以表彰他“对冰立方中微子观测站和发现天体物理起源的高能中微子做出的决定性贡献”。
